flatCases.title: Happy path: send OTP with a valid 10-digit number (mobile)
flatCases.preconditions: App freshly launched on Android, signed out, LoginScreen visible, valid test phone number with SMS reception.
steps: Type a valid 10-digit mobile number into the phone field (note the +91 prefix is fixed and non-editable).
Tap 'Send OTP →'.
Observe the button/progress state, then wait for the SMS.
flatCases.expected: Button disables, a LinearProgressIndicator appears while loading; on codeSent the app slides to OtpScreen showing 'sent to +91 NNxxx xxxxx' (first 2 digits visible, rest masked). An SMS with a 6-digit code arrives.

flatCases.title: Happy path: manual OTP entry + verify via on-screen keypad (mobile)
flatCases.preconditions: On OtpScreen (mobile, width < 900) after a successful Send OTP; valid 6-digit code received via SMS.
steps: Tap the on-screen numeric keypad to enter all 6 digits of the received code.
Confirm focus advances box-to-box and the last box stops advancing at index 5.
Tap 'Verify →'.
flatCases.expected: LinearProgressIndicator shows during sign-in; on success the screen fades (pushReplacement) to SuccessScreen ('you're in!'), then the gate resolves to AccountantShell. No error banner.

flatCases.title: Happy path: Android instant SMS auto-verify (verificationCompleted)
flatCases.preconditions: Android device/number where Firebase SMS auto-retrieval works; app on LoginScreen.
steps: Enter the valid 10-digit number and tap 'Send OTP →'.
Do NOT type the code; wait for Android to auto-retrieve the SMS.
flatCases.expected: verificationCompleted fires, signInWithCredential succeeds, and the app navigates to SuccessScreen WITHOUT visiting/typing on OtpScreen. (Note: this uses push not pushReplacement, so LoginScreen remains beneath — verify Back behavior after Success animation in the dedicated case.)

flatCases.title: Web: OTP entry via physical keyboard, Enter to verify (web/desktop)
flatCases.preconditions: App in a desktop browser at width >= 900; on OtpScreen with a valid code received on the phone bound to that number.
steps: Confirm the on-screen numeric keypad is NOT rendered (wide screen hides _NumKeypad).
Type the 6 digits on the physical keyboard (0-9 only).
Press Enter (or NumpadEnter).
flatCases.expected: Digits fill the boxes left-to-right; pressing Enter triggers _verify and signs in, fading to SuccessScreen then AccountantShell. Non-digit keys are ignored.

flatCases.title: Web: paste a 6-digit code via Ctrl/Cmd+V
flatCases.preconditions: On OtpScreen in a desktop browser; clipboard contains a string with at least 6 digits (e.g. '123456' or 'Your code is 123456').
steps: Copy a code containing >=6 digits to the clipboard.
Focus the OTP screen and press Ctrl+V (or Cmd+V on macOS).
Observe the boxes and focus index.
flatCases.expected: Non-digits are stripped; the first 6 digits populate all boxes, focus jumps to box 5. If the clipboard has fewer than 6 digits after stripping, the paste is ignored (no change).

flatCases.title: Mobile: paste code via keypad 'paste' function key
flatCases.preconditions: On OtpScreen on mobile (keypad visible); clipboard has >=6 digits.
steps: Copy a 6+ digit code to the clipboard.
Tap the 'paste' function key on the on-screen keypad.
flatCases.expected: Boxes fill with the first 6 digits, focus set to box 5. With <6 clipboard digits, nothing changes.

flatCases.title: Edge: phone shorter than 10 digits is rejected client-side
flatCases.preconditions: LoginScreen, signed out.
steps: Type a 9-digit number.
Tap 'Send OTP →'.
flatCases.expected: Inline error 'Enter a valid 10-digit number' shown; verifyPhoneNumber is NOT called; no SMS sent; not navigated to OtpScreen.

flatCases.title: Edge: 11+ digit / pasted non-digit phone is NOT rejected and flows to Firebase
flatCases.preconditions: LoginScreen. Validation is length<10 only — no exact-10 check, no inputFormatters, no digit-strip.
steps: Type or paste a 12-digit number (or content with spaces/letters making length >= 10).
Tap 'Send OTP →'.
flatCases.expected: Client passes validation and calls verifyPhoneNumber with '+91<raw>'. Firebase returns verificationFailed (invalid number) and the error message is shown. Confirm no crash and the loading state clears. (Documents weak validation / wasted SMS-quota risk.)

flatCases.title: Edge: +91 country code is hardcoded for every number
flatCases.preconditions: LoginScreen.
steps: Inspect the phone field — confirm there is no country-code picker and the '+91' prefix is a fixed, non-editable cell.
Enter a valid Indian 10-digit number and send OTP.
flatCases.expected: Number is always prefixed '+91'. A non-Indian number cannot be entered with a different country code (by design / limitation).

flatCases.title: Edge: Verify with fewer than 6 digits returns silently
flatCases.preconditions: On OtpScreen with 0-5 boxes filled.
steps: Enter only 4 digits.
Tap 'Verify →' (or press Enter on web).
flatCases.expected: _doVerify returns immediately with no spinner, no error, no network call — no feedback shown. (Documents the silent no-op.)

flatCases.title: Edge: OTP backspace clears current box then steps back
flatCases.preconditions: On OtpScreen with several digits entered.
steps: Fill boxes 0-3, leaving focus at box 4 (empty).
Press backspace/delete (web) or '⌫' key (mobile) once — focus box empty case.
Press backspace again.
flatCases.expected: First backspace on an empty focused box steps focus back one and clears that box; backspace on a filled focused box clears it in place without stepping back.

flatCases.title: Edge: tap a specific OTP box to re-target focus and overwrite
flatCases.preconditions: On OtpScreen with all 6 boxes filled.
steps: Tap box index 2 to move focus there.
Enter a new digit.
flatCases.expected: Focus moves to box 2 (active border/caret), the new digit overwrites box 2, then focus advances to box 3.

flatCases.title: Resend timer counts down 30s and reveals 'Resend code'
flatCases.preconditions: Just landed on OtpScreen.
steps: Observe the resend label immediately and over 30 seconds.
flatCases.expected: Shows 'resend in 0:30' counting down each second to 0:00, then switches to an underlined 'Resend code' link.

flatCases.title: BUG-WATCH: 'Resend code' link resets the timer but sends NO new SMS
flatCases.preconditions: On OtpScreen, countdown reached 0, original SMS not received (or expired).
steps: Tap the 'Resend code' link.
Wait for a new SMS.
flatCases.expected: Defect to flag: the link only restarts the 30s countdown (_startTimer); verifyPhoneNumber is NOT re-invoked so NO new SMS is sent. A user who never got the first code is stranded on this screen. Workaround: press Back to LoginScreen and Send OTP again (which uses forceResendingToken).

flatCases.title: Resend the real code by returning to LoginScreen (forceResendingToken)
flatCases.preconditions: On OtpScreen after a prior Send OTP (resendToken captured).
steps: Tap the back arrow (or device Back) to return to LoginScreen.
Tap 'Send OTP →' again with the same number.
flatCases.expected: verifyPhoneNumber is called again with forceResendingToken set, Firebase treats it as an explicit resend, a new SMS arrives, and a fresh OtpScreen opens with a new verificationId.

flatCases.title: Error: wrong OTP code shows specific error
flatCases.preconditions: On OtpScreen with a valid verificationId.
steps: Enter 6 digits that are NOT the correct code.
Tap 'Verify →'.
flatCases.expected: FirebaseAuthException 'invalid-verification-code' caught; error banner reads 'Wrong code. Check and try again'; spinner clears (_loading=false); user can retry.

flatCases.title: Error: expired/invalid verificationId (session-expired) shows generic error
flatCases.preconditions: On OtpScreen; leave it open long enough that the code/session expires (or otherwise force a non-invalid-code FirebaseAuthException such as session-expired).
steps: Enter any 6 digits after expiry.
Tap 'Verify →'.
flatCases.expected: Non-'invalid-verification-code' FirebaseAuthException maps to 'Verification failed. Try again'; spinner clears. (User must go back and resend.)

flatCases.title: BUG-WATCH: network drop during OTP verify hangs the spinner permanently
flatCases.preconditions: On OtpScreen with a valid code typed; ability to kill connectivity at the moment of Verify.
steps: Type the 6 correct digits.
Disable Wi-Fi/data (or use a network throttle to force a non-FirebaseAuthException error), then tap 'Verify →'.
flatCases.expected: Defect to flag: _doVerify only catches FirebaseAuthException, so a network/PlatformException is uncaught — _loading stays true, the button is stuck on a spinner, and NO error is shown. User cannot retry without restarting the app. (Confirm whether restoring network recovers.)

flatCases.title: Error: verificationFailed on Send OTP surfaces Firebase message
flatCases.preconditions: Conditions to trigger verificationFailed: e.g. SMS quota exceeded (too-many-requests), billing not enabled, or app-not-authorized.
steps: Repeatedly request OTPs (or use a test project with billing disabled) to trigger the failure.
Tap 'Send OTP →'.
flatCases.expected: verificationFailed callback fires; _loading clears; the inline error shows e.message (e.g. too-many-requests / billing-not-enabled text) or fallback 'Verification failed'. App does not navigate to OtpScreen and does not crash.

flatCases.title: Error: Android auto-verify sign-in failure
flatCases.preconditions: Android path where verificationCompleted fires but signInWithCredential fails (e.g. disabled account).
steps: Trigger Send OTP and let auto-verify fire while the account is in a failing state.
flatCases.expected: catch block sets _loading=false and error 'Auto-verification failed' on LoginScreen; no navigation to Success.

flatCases.title: Double-tap guard on Send OTP and Verify
flatCases.preconditions: LoginScreen / OtpScreen.
steps: Tap 'Send OTP →' twice rapidly.
On OtpScreen, after entering 6 digits, tap 'Verify →' twice rapidly.
flatCases.expected: While _loading is true the handlers early-return (no duplicate verifyPhoneNumber / signInWithCredential), and the disabled/spinner state prevents a second submit. No duplicate SMS or double sign-in attempt.

flatCases.title: Happy path: Success animation completes and hands off to Shell
flatCases.preconditions: Just signed in (manual verify path); SuccessScreen visible.
steps: Watch the 1400ms progress bar complete.
After it reaches 100%, press device/browser Back.
flatCases.expected: On AnimationStatus.completed, Navigator.popUntil(isFirst) discards Success/OTP/Login and lands on the reactive gate (AccountantShell). Pressing Back from the Shell exits the app (mobile) rather than returning to Login.

flatCases.title: Edge: after Android auto-verify, Login remains beneath Success (push vs pushReplacement)
flatCases.preconditions: Android auto-verify path (uses Navigator.push, not pushReplacement).
steps: Complete sign-in via auto-verify and let SuccessScreen finish.
Observe the back-stack behavior.
flatCases.expected: popUntil(isFirst) on Success completion still collapses the stack to the gate, so the user lands on the Shell and Back exits. Confirm there is no lingering LoginScreen reachable via Back. (Validates the push-not-pushReplacement difference is harmless.)

flatCases.title: Session restore on cold start with a persisted session (mobile)
flatCases.preconditions: Previously signed in on the device; app fully killed (swiped from recents).
steps: Relaunch the app from the launcher.
Observe the first screen(s).
flatCases.expected: StreamBuilder shows SplashScreen during ConnectionState.waiting, then authStateChanges emits the persisted User and the app opens directly to AccountantShell — no LoginScreen, no re-OTP.

flatCases.title: Session restore on web browser refresh
flatCases.preconditions: Signed in in a web browser tab.
steps: Press F5 / browser refresh on the app tab.
Observe the screens.
flatCases.expected: SplashScreen briefly during waiting, then the gate (auth stream, not a one-time currentUser read) restores the session and renders AccountantShell. User is NOT bounced to LoginScreen.

flatCases.title: Caches load on sign-in (auth side effect)
flatCases.preconditions: Signed out; Supabase reachable (yynuu/ztugw per env); stock/customers/vendors tables populated.
steps: Complete sign-in.
Navigate to a screen using stock/customers/vendors (e.g. stock picker, party list) and/or watch logs for the three cache fetches.
flatCases.expected: _wireSessionAndSentryUser listener fires on the non-null uid and calls StockItemsCache/CustomersCache/VendorsCache .fetch(); the three caches populate (stock paginates 1000-row pages). UI that depends on them is ready.

flatCases.title: Sign out clears caches and returns to Login
flatCases.preconditions: Signed in; on ProfileScreen.
steps: Tap 'Sign out'.
Observe navigation and re-check cached data screens.
flatCases.expected: FirebaseAuth.signOut() flips the auth stream to null; the gate renders LoginScreen at the base route (no manual navigation). The three caches are .clear()'d and Sentry user is nulled. Re-entering protected screens shows empty/reloading state.

flatCases.title: Auth re-emit of the same user does not reload caches (uid==lastUid guard)
flatCases.preconditions: Signed in; instrument or log cache .fetch() calls.
steps: Trigger an authStateChanges re-emission of the same user (e.g. token refresh / stream re-emit) without signing out.
Watch for redundant cache fetches.
flatCases.expected: Sentry scope is re-set, but because uid==lastUid the listener early-returns and the three caches are NOT re-fetched (no redundant Supabase load).

flatCases.title: Sentry scope is tagged with uid on sign-in and nulled on sign-out
flatCases.preconditions: Sentry DSN configured (non-empty) for the test build.
steps: Sign in, then trigger a captured backend failure (e.g. force a non-2xx call) and check the Sentry event.
Sign out, then trigger another captured failure.
flatCases.expected: Events while signed in carry SentryUser(id=uid); after sign-out the user is null on events. No phone number/PII is attached (sendDefaultPii=false).

flatCases.title: JWT attached as Bearer on backend calls (image stream / sync)
flatCases.preconditions: Signed in; a backend call path that uses ApiClient (e.g. GET push-queue image).
steps: Trigger an ApiClient.get/getBytes call (e.g. open a stored invoice image).
Capture the outgoing request headers (proxy/devtools network).
flatCases.expected: Headers include Authorization: Bearer <Firebase ID token> (from currentUser.getIdToken(), no forceRefresh), plus x-api-key=Config.mrpApiKey and a unique x-request-id. Backend requireApiKey verifies the Bearer JWT first.

flatCases.title: Backend 401 throws Unauthorized but does NOT sign the user out
flatCases.preconditions: Signed in; ability to force a 401 (e.g. revoke/disable the Firebase user server-side so a cached token is rejected, or point at a backend that rejects the key).
steps: Revoke the user or otherwise make the next ApiClient call return 401.
Trigger a backend call (image fetch / report / activate).
Observe app behavior.
flatCases.expected: ApiClient calls reportFailure to Sentry and throws Exception('Unauthorized'); the app does NOT auto-sign-out or route to Login — calls keep failing until a manual app restart. (Documents the no-re-auth risk; the failing call should surface a user-visible error rather than silently corrupt state.)

flatCases.title: Stale token after account disable: getIdToken uses no forceRefresh
flatCases.preconditions: Signed in with a cached, not-yet-expired ID token; disable/revoke the account in Firebase console.
steps: Immediately (before token expiry) trigger a backend call.
Then wait past the SDK token refresh window and trigger another call.
flatCases.expected: Because getIdToken() passes no forceRefresh, the first call may still send the stale (cached) token and could succeed/fail depending on backend revocation checks; once the SDK refreshes, verifyIdToken rejects -> 401 'Invalid or expired token'. App keeps showing protected UI (no forced logout).

flatCases.title: SECURITY: activate push-to-Tally is authenticated by x-api-key only (no Bearer JWT)
flatCases.preconditions: Knowledge that POST /api/sync/push-queue/activate is hand-rolled in voucher_detail_sheet.dart with x-api-key=Config.activateApiKey and no Authorization header.
steps: Trigger a voucher push and capture the activate request headers.
Separately, replay the activate POST with only the bundled x-api-key and NO Firebase Bearer (e.g. via curl) against the backend.
Confirm whether the call succeeds without a valid Firebase session.
flatCases.expected: Defect to flag: the highest-value action (queue a Tally voucher push) succeeds with only the shipped x-api-key and no user JWT — a signed-out or key-holding client can enqueue money-moving pushes. Confirm and document; recommend requiring the Bearer JWT here.

flatCases.title: SECURITY: reorder-levels ignores the Firebase JWT (requireClientApiKey only)
flatCases.preconditions: GET /api/sync/reorder-levels/:reportKey is gated by requireClientApiKey (x-api-key vs API_KEY_CLIENT) and ignores the Bearer JWT.
steps: Trigger the reorder/inventory report and capture headers.
Replay the request with only the client x-api-key and no JWT.
Replay again with a wrong/missing key.
flatCases.expected: With the correct client key the report returns regardless of Firebase identity; with a missing/mismatched key the middleware returns 401 'Unauthorized' (length-mismatch short-circuits before timingSafeEqual). Document that report data is gated by a shared embedded secret, not per-user identity.

flatCases.title: SECURITY: Firebase identity is not propagated to Supabase (anon key + RLS)
flatCases.preconditions: App initialized with Config.supabaseUrl + anon/publishable key; signed in.
steps: Capture a direct Supabase read (e.g. a cache fetch on stock_items/ledgers) and inspect the auth context.
Confirm no Firebase token is forwarded to Supabase.
flatCases.expected: Supabase calls use only the anon key under RLS — the Firebase JWT is never sent. The two trust contexts are independent; document that the embedded anon key + activate x-api-key alone suffice to read ledgers/stock and enqueue pushes.

flatCases.title: Concurrency: sign in on web while already signed in on mobile (independent sessions)
flatCases.preconditions: Same phone number; signed in on the mobile app.
steps: Open the web app and complete OTP sign-in with the same number.
Use both clients (e.g. open queue/profile) and confirm both remain authenticated.
flatCases.expected: Firebase phone auth allows the same user on multiple devices; both sessions are valid and independent. Each client loads its own caches. No session is invalidated by the other.

flatCases.title: Concurrency: signing out on one platform does not sign out the other
flatCases.preconditions: Signed in on both mobile and web with the same number.
steps: On mobile, tap Sign out.
On the web client (without refreshing), continue using the app, then refresh.
flatCases.expected: FirebaseAuth.signOut() is local to one device; the web session persists (Firebase persistence is per-client). Mobile returns to Login and clears its caches; web stays signed in until it independently signs out.

flatCases.title: Concurrency: phone document-scan in flight while web session is open (auth not disrupted)
flatCases.preconditions: Signed in on both; mobile starts an Android document scan / upload.
steps: On mobile, start a scan (inserts scan_jobs row).
Keep the web client open and idle, then refresh web.
Confirm both clients remain authenticated throughout.
flatCases.expected: Auth/session is unaffected by the scan flow; web refresh still restores the session via authStateChanges, and the mobile session stays valid while the scan/parse runs.

flatCases.title: Platform: numeric keypad visibility flips at the 900px breakpoint
flatCases.preconditions: On OtpScreen; ability to resize the window (web/desktop) or compare phone vs tablet/web.
steps: View OtpScreen at width < 900 (mobile).
View/resize to width >= 900 (desktop/web).
flatCases.expected: Below 900px the on-screen _NumKeypad is rendered; at/above 900px it is hidden and entry relies on the physical-keyboard Focus handler. The transition is clean with no overflow.

flatCases.title: Platform: web applies 1.4x text scaling app-wide including auth screens
flatCases.preconditions: App in a web browser.
steps: Open LoginScreen, OtpScreen, SuccessScreen, SplashScreen on web.
Compare text size against the same screens on mobile.
flatCases.expected: kIsWeb MediaQuery textScaler 1.4x makes all auth-screen text ~40% larger; no clipping/overlap of labels, error banners, OTP boxes, or buttons.

flatCases.title: Platform: web text is selectable/copyable via SelectionArea
flatCases.preconditions: Web browser, any auth screen.
steps: On LoginScreen/OtpScreen, drag-select the masked phone text or labels with the mouse.
Copy and paste elsewhere.
flatCases.expected: Displayed Text is selectable and copyable (SelectionArea wraps the gate), which is not Flutter web's default. Confirm no layout breakage from selection.

flatCases.title: Platform: web/iOS never auto-verify — always manual OTP entry
flatCases.preconditions: Web (or iOS) client; valid number.
steps: Send OTP and wait without typing.
Confirm no auto sign-in occurs, then type the code manually.
flatCases.expected: verificationCompleted does not fire on web/iOS (no SMS auto-retrieval); the user must manually enter the code on OtpScreen. Manual entry then signs in normally.

flatCases.title: Platform: Android-only document scanner blocked while still allowing auth
flatCases.preconditions: Signed in on web/iOS.
steps: Attempt to invoke the document scanner from the web client.
flatCases.expected: ML Kit scanner shows 'only available on Android'; this does not affect auth/session — the user stays signed in and can use other flows. (Confirms platform gating is scoped to the scanner, not auth.)

flatCases.title: Hot restart swallows Firebase 'duplicate-app' exception
flatCases.preconditions: Dev build; ability to hot-restart (or relaunch where native [DEFAULT] app stays registered).
steps: Trigger a hot restart of the running app.
Observe startup.
flatCases.expected: Firebase.initializeApp throws [core/duplicate-app]; main.dart swallows only that code and continues. App boots normally to Splash->gate; any other FirebaseException would rethrow.

flatCases.title: SplashScreen shown during auth-stream waiting state
flatCases.preconditions: Cold start or web refresh with slow auth-state resolution.
steps: Launch/refresh on a slow network or throttled device and watch the first frame.
flatCases.expected: While snapshot.connectionState == waiting, SplashScreen (fade animation, 3 progress dots) is shown; it is replaced by Shell (hasData) or Login (no data) once the stream emits. No flash of the wrong screen.

flatCases.title: Edge: masked phone display for short/edge inputs
flatCases.preconditions: Navigated to OtpScreen (requires Firebase to have accepted Send OTP).
steps: Reach OtpScreen with a normal 10-digit number and read the subtitle.
(If reachable) reach it with an unusual <2-digit raw — verify fallback.
flatCases.expected: Subtitle shows 'sent to +91 NNxxx xxxxx' with only the first 2 digits visible; if the cleaned phone has <2 digits it falls back to showing the raw phone. No full number is ever displayed.

flatCases.title: Back navigation from OtpScreen preserves number and stack
flatCases.preconditions: On OtpScreen reached from LoginScreen via Send OTP.
steps: Tap the in-screen back arrow (or device Back on mobile).
Observe LoginScreen state.
flatCases.expected: Returns to LoginScreen (the route beneath). The phone field retains its controller value; _resendToken is retained so a subsequent Send OTP is treated as a resend.

flatCases.title: Data-integrity: cache fetch on sign-in fails (Supabase down) does not break auth
flatCases.preconditions: Signed-in attempt while Supabase is unreachable or returns an error (e.g. block the Supabase host).
steps: Block Supabase connectivity, then complete sign-in.
Observe the app state and any error reporting.
flatCases.expected: Auth still succeeds and the Shell renders; the three cache .fetch() calls fail and are reported via reportHandledError to Sentry, leaving caches empty (dependent screens show empty/loading) — but the user is NOT blocked from being signed in. No crash; foreground resync should recover when Supabase returns.

flatCases.title: Loading affordances on Send OTP (button disabled + progress bar)
flatCases.preconditions: LoginScreen with a valid number entered.
steps: Tap 'Send OTP →' and observe the UI until codeSent/verificationFailed.
flatCases.expected: During _loading the Send OTP button renders disabled (muted, no shadow, tap ignored) and a LinearProgressIndicator is shown; both clear when the callback returns.

flatCases.title: Edge: keypad digit input ignored once all 6 boxes are filled (focus at 5)
flatCases.preconditions: On OtpScreen with all 6 digits entered (focus index at 5, last box filled).
steps: Enter another digit via keypad/keyboard.
flatCases.expected: Because _inputDigit advances focus only up to index 5, an extra digit overwrites box 5 in place (focus does not exceed 6); the code never exceeds 6 digits. Confirm overwrite behavior and that Verify uses the visible 6 digits.

flatCases.title: Open capture flow from bottom-nav center camera item shows Sale/Purchase dialog
flatCases.preconditions: Logged in; app on Queue screen (Android phone or web session).
steps: Tap the center camera item in the bottom-nav (index 2), or on web/desktop the equivalent side-rail capture entry
Observe the modal that appears
flatCases.expected: CaptureTypeDialog opens as a modal offering exactly two choices: Sale and Purchase. No scan_jobs row is created yet and the Processing badge does not change.

flatCases.title: Open capture flow from camera screen + button (onCaptureRequested(null)) shows dialog
flatCases.preconditions: Android phone, logged in, on Camera screen.
steps: Tap the small + button (bottom-right of the camera shutter row)
Observe
flatCases.expected: CaptureTypeDialog opens (preferredType is null so a type must be chosen). No badge change until a scan is sent.

flatCases.title: Tapping the shutter with an active capture type skips the dialog
flatCases.preconditions: Android phone; a capture type (e.g. Sale) already chosen so the 'Sale batch' chip shows on the Camera screen.
steps: Tap the large circular shutter button (which calls onCaptureRequested(activeCaptureType))
Observe
flatCases.expected: No CaptureTypeDialog appears; the document scanner opens directly using the already-selected type.

flatCases.title: Dismiss the capture type dialog without choosing
flatCases.preconditions: CaptureTypeDialog is open.
steps: Tap outside the dialog or press the system back button to dismiss it without selecting Sale or Purchase
Observe
flatCases.expected: Dialog returns null; flow returns early. No scanner opens, no scan_jobs row is inserted, no parse request is sent, the Processing badge is unchanged.

flatCases.title: Choose Sale routes to the sale parse URL and Sale badge tab
flatCases.preconditions: Android phone, logged in, Tally party + stock exist server-side for the invoice.
steps: Start capture, choose Sale
Complete a scan of a valid sale invoice
Watch the Queue Sale tab badge and (server-side) the parse target
flatCases.expected: Parse POST goes to Config.saleParseUrl (/?type=sale&push=queue) with &job_id=<row id> appended; the +1 Processing badge appears on the Sale tab; after parse, a sale push_queue row appears.

flatCases.title: Choose Purchase routes to the purchase parse URL and Purchase badge tab
flatCases.preconditions: Android phone, logged in.
steps: Start capture, choose Purchase
Complete a scan of a valid purchase invoice
Watch the Queue Purchase tab badge and parse target
flatCases.expected: Parse POST goes to Config.purchaseParseUrl (/docstrange?purchase=all&source=runpod) with &job_id appended; the Processing badge appears on the Purchase tab; after parse, a purchase push_queue row appears.

flatCases.title: Web blocks scanning with the Android-only snackbar
flatCases.preconditions: Logged in via web browser.
steps: Open the capture flow and choose Sale (or Purchase)
Observe
flatCases.expected: A snackbar 'Document scanning is only available on Android.' is shown; no scanner opens, no scan_jobs row is created, no parse request fires. The _activeCaptureType tag is set but has no functional effect.

flatCases.title: iOS blocks scanning with the Android-only snackbar
flatCases.preconditions: App running on iOS (if an iOS build is available).
steps: Open the capture flow and choose a type
Observe
flatCases.expected: Snackbar 'Document scanning is only available on Android.' shown; no scan, no scan_jobs row. (Gate is !kIsWeb && platform==android, so iOS is excluded.)

flatCases.title: Android passes the platform gate and opens the ML Kit scanner
flatCases.preconditions: Android phone with camera permission granted.
steps: Open capture flow, choose a type
Observe the native UI that launches
flatCases.expected: The Google ML Kit DocumentScanner opens (full mode, gallery-import enabled, pageLimit 20, jpeg+pdf formats).

flatCases.title: Successful scan adds a capture and fires the enqueue
flatCases.preconditions: Android phone; scanner open.
steps: Capture a document and confirm/finish in the scanner so a PDF is produced
Observe the capture tray thumbnail count and the processing snackbar
flatCases.expected: A CapturedShot is added (tray badge increments), the 'Your <type> voucher is being processed…' snackbar (2s) shows, a scan_jobs row is inserted and the parse POST is dispatched.

flatCases.title: Cancel the scanner produces no scan_jobs row and no stuck badge
flatCases.preconditions: Android phone; scanner open.
steps: Press cancel/back in the document scanner so it returns with no PDF (result.pdf?.uri is null/empty)
Return to the app and check the Queue Processing badge
flatCases.expected: Flow returns early: no CapturedShot, no scan_jobs row, no parse request, Processing badge unchanged. No stuck/phantom badge.

flatCases.title: Scanner permission denied / cannot open shows error snackbar and closes cleanly
flatCases.preconditions: Android phone with camera permission DENIED (revoke in system settings).
steps: Open capture flow and choose a type so the scanner attempts to launch
Observe
flatCases.expected: scanDocument throws and is caught; snackbar 'Could not open the document scanner. Check camera permission and try again.' is shown; scanner.close() runs in finally; no scan_jobs row, no parse.

flatCases.title: Scanner page limit of 20 is enforced
flatCases.preconditions: Android phone, scanner open.
steps: Attempt to scan more than 20 pages in one session
Observe the scanner behavior
flatCases.expected: The scanner caps the batch at 20 pages (pageLimit:20); the produced PDF contains at most 20 pages and the flow proceeds normally.

flatCases.title: Gallery import path produces a parseable PDF
flatCases.preconditions: Android phone with an invoice image/PDF in the gallery.
steps: Open the scanner, use the gallery-import option (isGalleryImport:true) to import an existing image
Finish so a PDF is produced
flatCases.expected: Imported document is converted to a PDF, a CapturedShot is added and the enqueue/parse fires exactly as for a live camera scan.

flatCases.title: Processing snackbar text matches the chosen type
flatCases.preconditions: Android phone.
steps: Scan once as Sale, note the snackbar
Scan once as Purchase, note the snackbar
flatCases.expected: Snackbar reads 'Your Sale voucher is being processed…' for sale and 'Your Purchase voucher is being processed…' for purchase, each visible ~2 seconds.

flatCases.title: startScan inserts scan_jobs row and badge climbs only once (optimistic + echo dedup)
flatCases.preconditions: Android phone, realtime connected.
steps: Perform one scan
Immediately watch the Sale/Purchase Processing count badge over the next few seconds
flatCases.expected: Badge increments by exactly +1 (the optimistic local add is deduped against the realtime INSERT echo by row id); it does NOT briefly show +2.

flatCases.title: startScan failure: parse still fires but without job_id (badge gap)
flatCases.preconditions: Android phone; force the scan_jobs INSERT to fail (e.g. block the Supabase REST host or use an invalid anon key) while leaving the parse host reachable.
steps: Perform a scan
Observe the badge and confirm via logs/network that the parse POST still goes out
flatCases.expected: startScan returns null, reportHandledError('supabase.scan_jobs.startScan') is logged; the parse POST is sent to the BASE url with NO &job_id; that scan shows no optimistic badge on this device.

flatCases.title: startScan returns null but row was actually inserted server-side: badge sticks to TTL
flatCases.preconditions: Simulate the case where the scan_jobs INSERT succeeds server-side but the response is lost (network drop on the reply), so the client treats it as null.
steps: Trigger a scan under the lossy-reply condition
Observe the badge climb via realtime echo and whether it ever drains
flatCases.expected: The realtime INSERT echo climbs the badge on every client, but the parser received no job_id so it can never DELETE that row; the badge stays elevated until the 300s TTL sweep clears it (no push_queue/badge correlation for that scan).

flatCases.title: Parse POST carries only Content-Type application/pdf and no auth header
flatCases.preconditions: Android phone; ability to inspect the outgoing request (proxy/log).
steps: Perform a scan
Capture the outgoing parse POST headers
flatCases.expected: Request contains header Content-Type: application/pdf and the raw PDF bytes; NO x-api-key and NO Authorization/Bearer header is present (app→parsing-service boundary is unauthenticated).

flatCases.title: Unauthenticated parse endpoint can be triggered by anyone with the URL
flatCases.preconditions: Tester knows the saleParseUrl/purchaseParseUrl; a sample PDF.
steps: From an unauthenticated tool (curl/Postman) POST a PDF with Content-Type application/pdf to the parse URL
Check whether a push_queue voucher row is created
flatCases.expected: Document this as a risk: the call is accepted with no API key/Bearer, the parser builds a voucher and inserts a push_queue row that can subsequently be pushed into TallyPrime. Confirms the only auth boundary is parsing-service→main-backend, not app→parsing-service.

flatCases.title: Parse upload non-2xx response is logged only, no user signal
flatCases.preconditions: Android phone; force the parsing service to return a non-2xx (e.g. point parse URL at an endpoint returning 500, or send an oversized/empty body causing 400 'Bad request size').
steps: Perform a scan that yields a non-2xx parse reply
Observe app UI
flatCases.expected: Only a debugPrint('Parse send failed: HTTP <code>') is logged; NO error toast/dialog is shown to the user; the badge remains (driven by scan_jobs, not the HTTP reply) and drains only at the 300s TTL.

flatCases.title: Parse upload 300s timeout is caught and does not abort server-side parse
flatCases.preconditions: Android phone; induce a parse cold-start / slow response > 300s.
steps: Scan an invoice when the parsing service is cold
Wait past 300s and observe the app and later the queue
flatCases.expected: The client http POST times out after 300s, logged via debugPrint only; the server-side parse continues and may still insert a push_queue row and delete the scan_jobs row later. The badge was already swept at 300s, so the row appears with no live badge (confusing but not data loss).

flatCases.title: PDF file read failure before upload is caught
flatCases.preconditions: Android phone; the scanned PDF file is removed/unreadable before sendScanToParser reads it (race or deleted temp file).
steps: Trigger a scan where the temp PDF is no longer readable when readAsBytes runs
Observe
flatCases.expected: File(pdfPath).readAsBytes throws, caught, logged via debugPrint; no crash. (Note: the scan_jobs row may already exist, so the badge will sit until the 300s TTL since no parse landed.)

flatCases.title: Happy path end-to-end: scan → parse → push_queue row → badge drains on every client
flatCases.preconditions: Android phone AND a web session both logged into the same Supabase project; invoice with a matchable party + stock.
steps: On the phone, scan a valid invoice
Watch both the phone and the web Processing badge climb
Wait for the parse to finish
flatCases.expected: Both clients show +1 immediately; when the parsing service inserts the push_queue row and DELETEs the scan_jobs row, both clients drain -1 within realtime latency and the new voucher row appears in the queue on both.

flatCases.title: SILENT INVOICE DROP: parse produces no voucher (no party/stock match)
flatCases.preconditions: Android phone; scan an invoice whose party name does not match any ledger and/or whose line items match no stock (so queue_response.skipped=true).
steps: Scan such an invoice
Watch the badge for ~5 minutes
Check the queue for any new row and check for any error message
flatCases.expected: No push_queue row is ever created and the scan_jobs row is NOT deleted; the badge silently drains at the 300s TTL with NO error toast, dialog, or record. Confirms the highest-risk gap: a scanned money document is lost with zero user signal.

flatCases.title: SILENT DROP on purchase: push_queue_request_payload not produced
flatCases.preconditions: Android phone; scan a purchase invoice the docstrange/RunPod pipeline cannot turn into a payload dict.
steps: Scan the unparseable purchase invoice
Wait past 300s; check queue and any error
flatCases.expected: skipped=true, no delete_scan_job, no push_queue row; badge drains at TTL with no user-facing error. Invoice silently lost.

flatCases.title: Backend push-queue ingest down: voucher never lands, scan_jobs not deleted
flatCases.preconditions: Stop/break the main backend push-queue ingest (so post_to_push_queue fails) while parsing still runs.
steps: Scan a valid invoice
Wait past 300s; check queue and badge
flatCases.expected: Parser cannot insert the push_queue row; the scan_jobs row is not deleted; badge drains only at the 300s TTL; no voucher appears and the user gets no error. Documented as silent loss when the ingest is unavailable.

flatCases.title: Exception in parser do_POST before delete leaves badge to TTL
flatCases.preconditions: Induce a parser-side exception after upload but before delete_scan_job (e.g. a corrupt PDF that crashes parsing).
steps: Scan the corrupt document
Observe badge and queue over 5 minutes
flatCases.expected: Parser returns an error payload; scan_jobs row is never deleted, no push_queue row created; badge sticks until the 300s TTL sweep clears it; no user-facing error.

flatCases.title: Malformed/non-UUID job_id reaching the parser makes delete a no-op
flatCases.preconditions: Craft a parse request whose &job_id is not a 36-char UUID (manual/test harness).
steps: POST a PDF to the parse URL with &job_id=not-a-uuid
Observe whether any scan_jobs DELETE happens
flatCases.expected: delete_scan_job fails the /[0-9a-fA-F-]{36}/ regex and is a no-op; if a corresponding scan_jobs row exists its badge relies on the 300s TTL to clear. No SQL injection via job_id.

flatCases.title: 5s TTL sweep clears a stuck badge after 300s
flatCases.preconditions: A scan_jobs row exists whose DELETE will never arrive (e.g. parse produced no voucher).
steps: Create the stuck condition (scan an unmatchable invoice)
Note the badge climb time
Wait just over 300s without backgrounding the app
flatCases.expected: At ~300s the periodic 5s _sweep drops the stale row and the Processing badge decrements to its correct value automatically, even though no DELETE was received.

flatCases.title: Foreground resync catches a DELETE missed while backgrounded
flatCases.preconditions: A scan is in flight; realtime socket will be suspended by backgrounding.
steps: Start a scan so the badge climbs
Background the app/tab (lock phone or switch browser tabs) and keep it backgrounded while the parse completes and the scan_jobs row is deleted
Bring the app/tab back to the foreground
flatCases.expected: On AppLifecycleState.resumed the app calls _scanService.resync() and pushQueueService.refresh(); the badge corrects to the true count and the new push_queue row appears, recovering the missed realtime DELETE.

flatCases.title: Initial subscribe fetches only rows newer than 300s
flatCases.preconditions: scan_jobs table contains both fresh (<300s) and stale (>300s) rows.
steps: Cold-start the app / recreate the shell so subscribe()/_refresh() runs
Observe the badge count
flatCases.expected: Only rows with created_at >= now-300s are loaded; stale rows are ignored so the badge reflects genuinely in-flight scans, not historical leftovers.

flatCases.title: Per-tab badge split: sale scan only affects Sale tab
flatCases.preconditions: Android phone on the Queue screen.
steps: Scan one Sale invoice
Switch between the Sale and Purchase tabs and read the Processing badge on each
flatCases.expected: countFor(sale) shows the +1 on the Sale tab only; the Purchase tab badge is unaffected (count is split by the row's type).

flatCases.title: Oldest-start drives the loading timer ring
flatCases.preconditions: At least one in-flight scan of a given type.
steps: Scan an invoice and open the Queue tab for that type
Watch the QueueLoadingTile ring
Scan a second of the same type a minute later
flatCases.expected: oldestStartFor returns the EARLIEST in-flight start; the looping step-timer ring is anchored to that oldest start and does not reset when a newer scan is added.

flatCases.title: Multiple concurrent in-flight scans increment the count correctly
flatCases.preconditions: Android phone.
steps: Scan three Sale invoices in quick succession (each parse still pending)
Read the Sale tab Processing count
flatCases.expected: The Sale Processing badge shows 3; as each parse completes (scan_jobs DELETE) the count decrements one at a time back toward 0.

flatCases.title: Phone scan climbs the badge on an already-open web session
flatCases.preconditions: Web session and an Android phone both logged into the SAME Supabase project; web on the Queue screen.
steps: On the phone, scan an invoice
Without touching the web session, watch its Processing badge
flatCases.expected: The web client's Processing badge climbs +1 via the scan_jobs_live INSERT echo even though the web client never scans, then drains -1 when the parse deletes the row.

flatCases.title: Two phones scanning simultaneously: every client sees the combined count
flatCases.preconditions: Two Android phones on the same project, plus optionally a web session.
steps: Have both phones scan a Sale invoice at nearly the same time
Read the Sale Processing count on each device
flatCases.expected: All clients converge to a count of 2 (sum of both scan_jobs rows); each drains independently as its parse completes.

flatCases.title: DUPLICATE ENQUEUE: double-tap capture creates two scan_jobs and two push_queue rows
flatCases.preconditions: Android phone.
steps: Scan the SAME invoice twice (or double-trigger the capture so two PDFs are produced)
Wait for both parses to complete and inspect the queue
flatCases.expected: Two scan_jobs rows and two parse requests are produced, yielding two push_queue voucher rows for the same invoice — a double-posting hazard. Confirms there is no client-side de-duplication of identical scans.

flatCases.title: DUPLICATE PURCHASE: invoice_exists flagged but voucher still enqueued
flatCases.preconditions: Android phone; a purchase invoice whose invoice number already exists in the system.
steps: Scan the already-existing purchase invoice
Inspect the resulting push_queue row and any duplicate flag
flatCases.expected: The purchase pipeline's duplicacy check sets invoice_exists=true but STILL enqueues the voucher; the duplicate is NOT blocked and relies on the user noticing the flag before pushing to Tally. Sales have no such gate at all.

flatCases.title: Capture tray opens with thumbnails after scanning
flatCases.preconditions: Android phone with at least one captured shot.
steps: Tap the capture-batch thumbnail stack on the Camera screen
Observe the modal
flatCases.expected: A bottom-sheet grid of CapturedShot tiles opens showing the file name, type label ('Sale/Purchase receipt') and capture index, with a 'N shots' count matching the number of captures.

flatCases.title: Capture tray no-op when empty
flatCases.preconditions: Android phone with no captures (fresh shell).
steps: Tap the capture-batch thumbnail stack
Observe
flatCases.expected: Nothing happens (early return when captures is empty); no modal opens.

flatCases.title: Save PDF from tray succeeds
flatCases.preconditions: Android phone with a captured shot; storage writable.
steps: Open the capture tray, tap the download icon on a thumbnail
Choose a save location in the file picker and confirm
flatCases.expected: File is written as challan_<type>_<timestamp>.pdf and a 'PDF saved' snackbar appears.

flatCases.title: Save PDF failure shows error snackbar
flatCases.preconditions: Android phone; induce a save failure (e.g. cancel into an unwritable location or remove the source temp file).
steps: Open the tray, tap download on a thumbnail, trigger the failure
Observe
flatCases.expected: A 'Save failed: <error>' snackbar is shown; the app does not crash.

flatCases.title: Captures are in-memory and cleared when the shell is recreated
flatCases.preconditions: Android phone with several captures in the tray.
steps: Note the capture count
Force the shell to be recreated (e.g. navigate in a way that rebuilds AccountantShell, or the scanner teardown recreates it)
Reopen the Camera screen and check the tray
flatCases.expected: The _captures list is empty (it lives only on app_shell in memory); the in-flight scan_jobs badge, however, persists because it is mirrored from Supabase, not from _captures.

flatCases.title: Web has no capture tray and never produces captures
flatCases.preconditions: Web session.
steps: Navigate to the Camera screen on web
Attempt to open the capture tray / look for thumbnails
flatCases.expected: No captures exist on web (the scan flow that populates _captures is Android-only and uses dart:io File); the tray is always empty and Save-PDF is unavailable.

flatCases.title: Web observes badge changes but never inserts a scan_jobs row
flatCases.preconditions: Web session logged in with no phone scanning.
steps: On web, open the capture flow and choose a type (hits the Android-only gate)
Confirm via DB/realtime that no scan_jobs row was created by the web client
flatCases.expected: Web never calls startScan; it only subscribes to scan_jobs_live and reflects rows created by mobile clients. No web-originated scan_jobs row.

flatCases.title: Web refresh restores session and re-subscribes to the badge
flatCases.preconditions: Web session with an in-flight scan visible (started from a phone).
steps: Refresh the browser tab (F5)
After the session restores via authStateChanges, observe the Processing badge
flatCases.expected: Session is restored on web refresh; ScanJobsService.subscribe()/_refresh() re-runs and the badge correctly reflects the current in-flight scan_jobs rows (initial fetch + resubscribe), not a stale or zeroed value.

flatCases.title: Web 1.4x text scaling does not clip the processing snackbar / badge
flatCases.preconditions: Web session.
steps: Trigger badge-related UI (have a phone start a scan so the web badge + loading tile render)
Inspect the QueueLoadingTile text and any snackbar at the web 1.4x scaling
flatCases.expected: Text renders at 1.4x scale without truncation or overlap; the Processing count and timer ring remain legible.

flatCases.title: Web desktop breakpoint (>=900) shows side-rail and does not break the loading tile
flatCases.preconditions: Web at a window width >= 900px.
steps: Have a phone start a scan so the badge climbs
Confirm the desktop layout: bottom-nav replaced by a side-rail; check the loading tile renders
Resize below 900px and confirm it switches back to bottom-nav
flatCases.expected: At >=900px the layout uses the side-rail (two-pane behavior available elsewhere) and the Processing loading tile/badge still render correctly; below 900px it reverts to the bottom-nav.

flatCases.title: Cold-start parse exceeding 300s: row appears later without a live badge
flatCases.preconditions: Parsing service is cold so the round-trip exceeds 300s for one invoice.
steps: Scan a valid invoice while the service is cold
Watch the badge cross the 300s mark (it sweeps to 0)
Keep the app open and wait for the parse to finish later
flatCases.expected: Badge is swept at 300s (no in-flight indicator), then the push_queue voucher row appears with no accompanying Processing badge. The voucher is not lost but the badge/reality desync is observable.

flatCases.title: created_at unparseable falls back to now() (badge still counts)
flatCases.preconditions: Ability to inject a scan_jobs row with a null/invalid created_at (test harness).
steps: Insert/echo a scan_jobs row with a malformed created_at
Observe the badge
flatCases.expected: _toJob falls back to DateTime.now() so the row is treated as fresh and counted; it will be swept 300s after the fallback time. No crash from the bad timestamp.

flatCases.title: scan_jobs RLS is fully permissive — multi-company project would leak badges
flatCases.preconditions: Knowledge of the scan_jobs RLS policy (FOR ALL USING(true) WITH CHECK(true)); single-project-per-client assumed.
steps: Review the policy and confirm there is no company_id scoping on scan_jobs
Reason about a hypothetical multi-company project
flatCases.expected: Document that isolation relies entirely on one-Supabase-project-per-client; if a project ever held multiple companies, every client would see every company's Processing badge. No per-row tenant scoping exists.

flatCases.title: Company coupling: parsed voucher is filed under the server-default company
flatCases.preconditions: Android phone where the operator's intended company differs from the parser's default (DEFAULT_PURCHASE_COMPANY / options company_name).
steps: Scan an invoice intended for company B while the parser default resolves to company A
Inspect the resulting push_queue row's company
flatCases.expected: Document the risk: the company is derived server-side, not from the scanning client; a mismatch files the voucher under the wrong company and is not validated in the scan→parse client path.

flatCases.title: Testing (yynuu) vs prod (ztugw): scans do not cross projects
flatCases.preconditions: One client pointed at testing Supabase (yynuu), another at prod (ztugw).
steps: Scan an invoice from the testing-configured client
Watch the prod-configured client's Processing badge and queue
flatCases.expected: The prod client's badge and queue are unaffected (scan_jobs/realtime are per-project); scans are isolated to the configured Supabase project.

flatCases.title: job_id appends correctly because both base URLs already contain '?'
flatCases.preconditions: Android phone; ability to inspect the outgoing parse URL.
steps: Scan a Sale invoice and capture the full request URL
Scan a Purchase invoice and capture the full request URL
flatCases.expected: Sale URL ends '...?type=sale&push=queue&job_id=<uuid>' and Purchase URL ends '...?purchase=all&source=runpod&job_id=<uuid>' — the bare '&job_id=' append is valid only because each base already has a query string. Flag that a future base URL without '?' would be malformed.

flatCases.title: Oversized PDF returns parser 400 'Bad request size' and is logged only
flatCases.preconditions: Android phone; a scanned PDF larger than the parser's MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES (or craft an empty/zero-length body).
steps: Send an over-limit (or empty) PDF to the parse endpoint
Observe the app and the badge
flatCases.expected: Parser returns 400 ('Bad request size' when Content-Length<=0 or > MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES); the app logs the non-2xx via debugPrint only, shows no user error, and the scan_jobs row (if created) drains at the 300s TTL.

flatCases.title: Phone goes offline after scan but before parse completes
flatCases.preconditions: Android phone; airplane mode toggled right after the scan_jobs INSERT succeeds and the parse POST is in flight.
steps: Scan an invoice
Immediately enable airplane mode so the parse upload cannot complete from this device
Re-enable connectivity after a minute and observe
flatCases.expected: The parse upload fails/times out (logged); since the parsing service may not have received the PDF, no push_queue row is created and the scan_jobs row drains at the 300s TTL. Foreground resync on reconnect corrects the badge. Invoice may be silently lost (no retry).

flatCases.title: Realtime DELETE drains the exact row by id (not all rows)
flatCases.preconditions: Two in-flight scans of different types (one Sale, one Purchase).
steps: Let the Sale parse complete first (its scan_jobs row is deleted) while the Purchase scan is still in flight
Read both tab badges
flatCases.expected: Only the Sale badge decrements (removeById matches the deleted row's id); the Purchase badge remains at its in-flight count. A DELETE removes exactly one row by id.

flatCases.title: Non-Android batch chip is cosmetic on web
flatCases.preconditions: Web session.
steps: Open the capture flow on web, choose Purchase (hits the gate)
Navigate to the Camera screen and observe the 'Purchase batch' chip
flatCases.expected: The _activeCaptureType chip/label may render but no scanning occurs; the tag has no functional effect on web beyond the cosmetic label.

flatCases.title: Initial queue load renders active rows sorted newest-first, grouped by day
flatCases.preconditions: Signed in. push_queue contains several rows with status pending/push_now/failed spanning Today, Yesterday, and an older date; at least one 'pushed' row also exists.
steps: Launch the app (mobile) or open the web URL and sign in.
Navigate to the Queue screen and stay on the Sale tab, then switch to Purchase tab.
flatCases.expected: Only rows with status pending/push_now/failed appear; the 'pushed' row is NOT in the queue. Rows are grouped under 'Today', 'Yesterday', then '<d Mon>' headers, each group ordered newest-first by created_at. Serial numbers run 1..N continuously across the whole active tab (not restarting per day group). Each row shows party name, abs(first ledger amount), time label.

flatCases.title: Sign-in subscribes to realtime and seeds the queue once
flatCases.preconditions: Signed out. push_queue has active rows.
steps: Sign in with phone OTP.
Open the Queue screen immediately after the shell loads.
flatCases.expected: subscribe() runs refresh() first then attaches push_queue_live INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE handlers; the queue populates from the initial select with no duplicate rows and no flicker of empty-then-full beyond the single load.

flatCases.title: Empty queue shows no rows and remains scroll/refresh-capable
flatCases.preconditions: push_queue has zero active rows for the signed-in tenant.
steps: Open the Queue screen.
Pull down to refresh.
flatCases.expected: Both Sale and Purchase tabs render empty (no day groups, no rows). The list still accepts the pull-to-refresh gesture (AlwaysScrollableScrollPhysics) and no error/crash occurs.

flatCases.title: refresh() failure (network down) leaves queue stale and reports to Sentry, no crash
flatCases.preconditions: Queue already showing rows.
steps: Disable network / block the Supabase host.
Pull to refresh on the Queue screen.
Re-enable network and pull to refresh again.
flatCases.expected: No crash and no user-facing error banner; the previously loaded rows stay visible (list left as-is). reportHandledError('supabase.push_queue.refresh') fires to Sentry. After network returns, refresh re-fetches and the list reconciles.

flatCases.title: Multi-client realtime INSERT: scan on phone appears in web queue
flatCases.preconditions: Same tenant signed in on an Android phone AND a web browser, both on the Queue screen (Purchase tab).
steps: On the phone, scan a purchase invoice (parsing service eventually inserts a push_queue row).
Watch the web session without refreshing.
flatCases.expected: When the parsing service inserts the push_queue row, the push_queue_live INSERT echo prepends the new row on BOTH the phone and the web session live (no manual refresh). The row appears at the top of its day group.

flatCases.title: Realtime INSERT with status 'pushed' is ignored by the queue
flatCases.preconditions: Queue open. Ability to insert a push_queue row already at status='pushed' (e.g. via parsing/back-office).
steps: Insert a push_queue row with status='pushed' directly.
Observe the live queue.
flatCases.expected: isActiveStatus() guard rejects it; the row does NOT appear in the live queue (it belongs to History). It surfaces only on the History screen via history_push_queue.

flatCases.title: Realtime INSERT has no dedup-by-id: redelivered/echoed INSERT can duplicate a row
flatCases.preconditions: Queue open showing a row that was already loaded by refresh().
steps: Trigger a duplicate INSERT echo for an id already present (e.g. force a reconnect/replay or insert a row whose id collides with one already loaded by refresh).
Observe the queue list.
flatCases.expected: DEFECT WATCH: the INSERT handler prepends without checking for an existing id (unlike scan_jobs._add), so the same row can appear twice until the next authoritative refresh() collapses it. Document whether a real duplicate row is observed.

flatCases.title: Realtime UPDATE pending->push_now keeps the row visible in the queue
flatCases.preconditions: A pending row visible in the queue.
steps: Push the row to Tally (or have the backend flip it) so status goes pending->push_now.
Watch the queue without closing the sheet.
flatCases.expected: The row stays visible (only 'pushed' removes it). Status reflects push_now. The row does not vanish-and-reappear.

flatCases.title: Realtime UPDATE to 'pushed' removes the row from the queue and it lands in History
flatCases.preconditions: A push_now row whose desktop push succeeds.
steps: Wait for the desktop poller to push the voucher to TallyPrime and flip status to 'pushed'.
Observe the Queue and then open History.
flatCases.expected: push_queue_live UPDATE with status=='pushed' removes the row from the live queue on every client; the row appears in History (history_push_queue), ordered by pushed_at desc.

flatCases.title: DATA INTEGRITY: TOASTed voucher_payload omitted on push_now UPDATE corrupts row to Unknown/₹0/Purchase
flatCases.preconditions: A pending SALE row visible on the Sale tab; backend will flip it to push_now updating only status+error_message.
steps: Activate the row so the backend UPDATE sets status=push_now and clears error_message (leaving the large voucher_payload column unchanged, so Realtime omits it).
Watch the queue row at the moment the realtime UPDATE echo arrives (before any refresh/onPushed reconcile).
flatCases.expected: DEFECT WATCH: unlike History (which re-fetches on empty payload), the queue UPDATE handler does NOT re-fetch. rowToEntry parses an empty payload so the row momentarily renders party 'Unknown', amount ₹0, and type defaulting to Purchase — a SALE row can jump to the Purchase tab — until onPushed/refresh reconciles it. Record the transient corruption.

flatCases.title: Realtime UPDATE omitting edit_state preserves the prior tag (column-cache lag)
flatCases.preconditions: A row already tagged 'under edit' or 'invoice edited' in the visible queue.
steps: Trigger an UPDATE to that row whose echo omits the edit_state column (e.g. a backend status flip).
Observe the row's tag chip.
flatCases.expected: Because the row already exists and the payload lacks the edit_state key, the handler re-applies the prior editState; the 'under edit'/'invoice edited' tag is NOT wiped. A subsequent refresh() confirms the tag from PostgREST authoritatively.

flatCases.title: Realtime UPDATE for an unknown (not-yet-loaded) id prepends it to the queue
flatCases.preconditions: Queue open; a row exists in Supabase that this client has not loaded (e.g. missed its INSERT).
steps: Issue a non-pushed UPDATE (e.g. edit_state change) to that unseen pending row.
Observe the queue.
flatCases.expected: The UPDATE handler upserts: since the id is unknown it prepends the row, so the queue self-heals and shows it even though the original INSERT was missed.

flatCases.title: Realtime DELETE removes the row on all clients
flatCases.preconditions: Same tenant signed in on two clients, both showing the same queue row.
steps: On client A, open the row and Delete it (or delete the push_queue row directly).
Observe client B without refreshing.
flatCases.expected: push_queue_live DELETE fires on client B; the row with id 'supabase_<deletedId>' is filtered out and disappears from B's queue live.

flatCases.title: Pull-to-refresh re-fetches authoritative rows and corrects any realtime drift
flatCases.preconditions: Queue showing rows where one is momentarily mis-rendered (e.g. from a payload-omitted echo) or out of order.
steps: Pull down on the Queue list to trigger RefreshIndicator (widget.onRefresh = PushQueueService.refresh).
Observe the rows after the spinner completes.
flatCases.expected: refresh() re-selects active rows and replaces _entries wholesale; any drift (Unknown/₹0, missing edit_state, stale order) is corrected from PostgREST. checked/status are preserved per id by the shell merge.

flatCases.title: Foreground resume re-syncs both queue and scan badge after backgrounding
flatCases.preconditions: App/tab backgrounded long enough for the realtime socket to suspend; while backgrounded another client inserts/deletes a push_queue row and a scan_jobs row.
steps: Background the app (mobile home button) or switch away from the web tab for ~1 minute while events occur on another client.
Return to the foreground / re-focus the tab.
Observe the queue and the Processing badge.
flatCases.expected: didChangeAppLifecycleState(resumed) calls _scanService.resync() and _pushQueueService.refresh(); rows and the scan badge catch up to the events missed while the socket was suspended (which are NOT replayed by realtime).

flatCases.title: Close mid-edit tags row 'under edit', floats it to top, persists edit_state
flatCases.preconditions: A pending row in the queue.
steps: Open the row, tap Edit, change something, then close the sheet WITHOUT saving (tap X / swipe down).
Observe the row in the queue.
flatCases.expected: Local _editMarkers tags it 'under edit' immediately; _persistEditState writes edit_state='under_edit' and bumps created_at=now(); after the write widget.onRefresh() reconciles so the 'under edit' tag and the float-to-top land durably. The row moves to the top of the Today group.

flatCases.title: Save edits tags row 'invoice edited', floats to top, persists
flatCases.preconditions: A pending row in the queue.
steps: Open the row, tap Edit, change an item, tap Save, then close the sheet.
Observe the row in the queue.
flatCases.expected: Row is tagged 'invoice edited' (everSaved), edit_state='edited' with created_at bumped; onRefresh reconciles so the tag persists and the row floats to the top of Today.

flatCases.title: View-then-close an untagged row writes nothing
flatCases.preconditions: An untagged pending row.
steps: Open the row, do not touch Edit, close the sheet.
Open it again, tap Edit, then immediately Revert back to original, close.
flatCases.expected: First close: touched=false so no write and no tag. Second close: edited-then-reverted on an untagged row clears the marker but, because the row was untagged when opened (marker==none), NO server write fires (no spurious update / no float-to-top).

flatCases.title: Clearing a tag writes edit_state=NULL without bumping created_at
flatCases.preconditions: A row currently tagged 'under edit' or 'invoice edited'.
steps: Open the tagged row, tap Edit then Revert to original (back to untagged), close the sheet.
Inspect the row order and tag.
flatCases.expected: _persistEditState(none, bump:false) writes edit_state=NULL with NO created_at bump; the tag clears but the row keeps its original position rather than floating to top.

flatCases.title: DATA INTEGRITY: edit float-to-top bump rewrites created_at, relocating an old voucher into Today
flatCases.preconditions: A pending voucher whose created_at is several days old (shows under an older date group).
steps: Open the old voucher, tap Edit, save (or close mid-edit), close the sheet.
Observe which day group the voucher now appears under.
flatCases.expected: DEFECT WATCH: created_at is reused as both sort key and day-group key; the bump to now() relocates the voucher into 'Today', misrepresenting when the invoice was actually captured. Confirm the day label changes from the real capture date to Today.

flatCases.title: Edit save on a pending row persists voucher_payload and confirms
flatCases.preconditions: A pending row.
steps: Open the row, tap Edit, change party/items/qty/rate, tap Save.
Observe the snackbar and reopen the row.
flatCases.expected: update push_queue set voucher_payload=cleanPayload .eq(id).eq(status,'pending') returns 1 row; snackbar 'Changes saved.'; __-prefixed keys are stripped from the persisted payload; reopening shows the edited values.

flatCases.title: Edit save on a row already push_now/pushed returns 0 rows -> 'already queued' message
flatCases.preconditions: A row that flipped to push_now (or pushed) after the sheet was opened, OR concurrently activated from another client.
steps: Open a pending row, enter Edit. From another client (or backend) flip the same row to push_now.
Tap Save on the first client.
flatCases.expected: The .eq(status,'pending') guard matches 0 rows; snackbar 'Couldn't save — this voucher may already be queued for push.' No payload change is persisted.

flatCases.title: Edit save throws (RLS/permission/network) -> Sentry + generic snackbar
flatCases.preconditions: A pending row; ability to force the update to throw (block network or simulate RLS denial).
steps: Open the row, Edit, make a change, disable network, tap Save.
flatCases.expected: reportHandledError('supabase.push_queue.update') fires; snackbar 'Couldn't save changes. Please try again.' The user is told it failed (but note: a swallowed RLS denial would still show the same generic message — verify the row is unchanged server-side).

flatCases.title: Push is blocked when party changed but not all items changed
flatCases.preconditions: A pending voucher with multiple items.
steps: Open the row, Edit, change the party (vendor/customer) but leave at least one item name unchanged, Save, then tap Push To Tally.
flatCases.expected: _partyNameWasChanged && !_allItemsDifferentFromOriginal is true: the Push button is dimmed (green at 0.45 alpha) and tapping it shows snackbar 'Party Name is Changed!!\nChange all the items'. No activate POST is sent. Same guard fires on Enter-on-Total (_submitFromTotal).

flatCases.title: Happy push: pending SALE -> activate -> push_now -> pushed shows success dialog and drops to History
flatCases.preconditions: Pending SALE row; desktop TallyBridge online and TallyPrime reachable.
steps: Open the SALE row, tap Push To Tally, confirm in the dialog.
Wait for the desktop to push and the realtime result to arrive.
flatCases.expected: Pre-push: voucher_payload persisted (narration overwritten to 'Replara AI'), POST /api/sync/push-queue/activate returns 2xx, button keeps spinner (_awaitingPushResult). Backend flips pending->push_now. vd_status_<rowId> UPDATE reports status 'pushed' or tally_response.created>=1. onPushed re-fetches; after the sheet closes a _SalePushedDialog shows customer/amount/pushed-at. The row leaves the queue and appears in History.

flatCases.title: DATA INTEGRITY: every push overwrites narration to fixed 'Replara AI'
flatCases.preconditions: A pending voucher whose parsed/edited narration is a meaningful description (e.g. real invoice notes).
steps: Open the row, optionally edit narration to a custom string, Save.
Tap Push To Tally and confirm.
Inspect the persisted voucher_payload.narration and the resulting TallyPrime voucher narration.
flatCases.expected: DEFECT WATCH: _activate unconditionally sets clean['narration']='Replara AI' before activating, destroying the parsed/edited narration. The pushed Tally voucher loses its real description/audit text. Confirm the custom narration is gone.

flatCases.title: Sale push failure shows the fail dialog with the Tally error
flatCases.preconditions: Pending SALE row; desktop push will fail (e.g. ledger mismatch in Tally).
steps: Push the SALE row to Tally and confirm.
Wait for the desktop to report failure (status=failed or created==0 && errors>=1).
flatCases.expected: _handlePushResult treats it as failed; the sheet closes and _SalePushFailedDialog shows error_message (or 'Push to Tally failed.' when empty). The row STAYS in the queue with status 'failed'.

flatCases.title: Purchase push closes the sheet silently with no result modal
flatCases.preconditions: Pending PURCHASE row; desktop reachable.
steps: Open the PURCHASE row, Push To Tally, confirm, wait for the result.
flatCases.expected: On terminal result the sheet closes and onPushed re-fetches; NO success/fail dialog is shown for purchase (sale-only). A pushed purchase drops to History; a failed one stays in the queue.

flatCases.title: DATA INTEGRITY: duplicate purchase invoice is only flagged visually and can still be pushed twice
flatCases.preconditions: Two purchase rows with the same voucher_payload.reference (same supplier invoice number) in the queue.
steps: On the Purchase tab, confirm the newer row shows the 'Duplicate: Already Exists In Queue' tag and is dimmed.
Open the dimmed duplicate row and tap Push To Tally, confirm.
Check TallyPrime for the result.
flatCases.expected: DEFECT WATCH: isQueueDuplicate is purely visual; the push is NOT blocked. The same supplier invoice can be activated and double-posted into TallyPrime. Confirm a second voucher is created.

flatCases.title: Activate returns 404 (job not found) -> failure snackbar
flatCases.preconditions: A queue row whose push_queue id has been deleted server-side after the sheet opened.
steps: Open the row, delete the underlying push_queue row from another client, then tap Push To Tally and confirm.
flatCases.expected: Backend returns 404 'Push queue job not found'. App shows snackbar 'Failed (404): Push queue job not found', clears the spinner (_isSubmitting=false), ApiClient.reportFailure logs the POST failure with x-request-id.

flatCases.title: Activate returns 409 (not pending) -> failure snackbar
flatCases.preconditions: A row that another client/desktop has already moved to push_now/pushed/failed.
steps: Open a row that looks pending locally; concurrently flip it to push_now elsewhere.
Tap Push To Tally and confirm.
flatCases.expected: Backend returns 409 'Push queue job must be pending before activation (current status: X)'. App shows 'Failed (409): ...', spinner clears. No double-activation.

flatCases.title: Activate lost-race returns 409 'could not be activated' (TOCTOU)
flatCases.preconditions: Two clients open the same pending row and push near-simultaneously.
steps: On client A and client B, tap Push To Tally and confirm at nearly the same time.
flatCases.expected: The backend update is guarded .eq(status,'pending'); the winner flips it to push_now, the loser's update matches 0 rows and returns 409 'Push queue job could not be activated'. Exactly one activation occurs (no double push).

flatCases.title: Activate returns 500 (Supabase lookup/update error) -> failure snackbar
flatCases.preconditions: Force a backend Supabase error on activate (e.g. simulated DB outage).
steps: Tap Push To Tally and confirm while the backend's Supabase is failing.
flatCases.expected: Backend returns 500 with an error body; app shows 'Failed (500): <body>', clears spinner, reports the failure to Sentry/ApiClient with the request id.

flatCases.title: Network error / timeout during activate POST -> error snackbar, spinner cleared
flatCases.preconditions: A pending row.
steps: Disable network (or block the activate host).
Tap Push To Tally, confirm.
flatCases.expected: The pre-push voucher_payload update may also fail; the POST throws. catch shows snackbar 'Error: <e>', clears _isSubmitting, and ApiClient.reportFailure logs error+stack with the request id. No partial 'pushing…' hang.

flatCases.title: Push while in edit mode prompts Save-before-push (no activate sent)
flatCases.preconditions: A pending row opened with unsaved edits (edit mode on).
steps: Open the row, tap Edit, change something (do not Save), tap Push To Tally.
flatCases.expected: _confirmAndActivate sees _isEditing and shows the _SaveBeforePushDialog; tapping OK just dismisses it (no save, no activate). The user must Save first, then Push follows the normal flow. No POST is sent while editing.

flatCases.title: Push confirm dialog Cancel aborts the push
flatCases.preconditions: A pending row.
steps: Tap Push To Tally, then tap Cancel/No in the confirm dialog.
flatCases.expected: No voucher_payload write, no activate POST; the sheet stays open unchanged, button not spinning.

flatCases.title: Enter-on-Total field triggers push with the same guards as the button
flatCases.preconditions: A pending row; physical/soft keyboard available (primarily web/desktop).
steps: Open the row, focus the Total field at the end of the Enter-to-move chain, press Enter.
flatCases.expected: _submitFromTotal runs: respects _isSubmitting, applies the party-changed/items guard (snackbar if blocked), otherwise runs _confirmAndActivate exactly like the Push button.

flatCases.title: Terminal result already arrived before activate POST returns is resolved immediately
flatCases.preconditions: A fast desktop that pushes and flips status to pushed before the activate HTTP response returns.
steps: Push a row where the vd_status UPDATE (pushed) lands before the POST resolves.
flatCases.expected: After 2xx, _activate checks _status=='pushed'/'failed' and calls _handlePushResult immediately with the captured status, rather than hanging in 'pushing…' waiting for an event already consumed.

flatCases.title: Push-result hang: errors>=1 with created==null and status not 'failed' stays in 'pushing…'
flatCases.preconditions: Ability to write a tally_response with errors>=1 but created==null while leaving status not 'failed'.
steps: Activate a row, then have the desktop write tally_response={errors:1} (no 'created' key) and NOT set status='failed'.
Observe the sheet.
flatCases.expected: DEFECT WATCH: _handlePushResult resolves only on success (pushed/created>=1) or failed (failed / created==0 && errors>=1). With created==null the failed branch is false, so the sheet stays stuck in 'pushing…' with the spinner indefinitely until manually closed.

flatCases.title: Async push result is delivered over the per-voucher vd_status channel while the sheet is open
flatCases.preconditions: A row sheet kept open after activate.
steps: Push the row, keep the sheet open, watch the Status chip and Push Details block update.
flatCases.expected: vd_status_<rowId> UPDATE updates _status, _pushedAt, _errorMessage in place; the header Status chip changes colour (amber push_now -> green pushed / red failed) and the Push Details block appears on terminal status.

flatCases.title: Narration-overwrite update in _activate is NOT guarded by status='pending'
flatCases.preconditions: A row that the backend may be transitioning concurrently.
steps: Trigger _activate while the backend is mid-transition on the same row (race the pre-push voucher_payload write against a status flip).
flatCases.expected: DEFECT WATCH: unlike _persistEditsToSupabase, the _activate pre-push update is only .eq(id) with no .eq(status,'pending'); it can rewrite voucher_payload (narration='Replara AI') on a row already moving to push_now. Safe only because the app only invokes it from pending UI. Document any payload rewrite on a non-pending row.

flatCases.title: Discard/Delete a queued row removes it locally then deletes server-side, syncing other clients
flatCases.preconditions: Two clients showing the same pending row.
steps: On client A, open the row, tap Delete, confirm in the dialog.
Observe client A and client B.
flatCases.expected: Client A drops the row from the in-memory list and pops the sheet immediately; then delete push_queue .eq(id) runs and shows 'Deleted.'. Client B receives the realtime DELETE and removes the row.

flatCases.title: Delete failure reports to Sentry and the row reappears on next refresh
flatCases.preconditions: A pending row; force the delete to throw (block network or RLS deny).
steps: Open the row, disable network, tap Delete, confirm.
Re-enable network and pull to refresh.
flatCases.expected: Local list drops the row and the sheet closes optimistically; the delete throws -> reportHandledError('supabase.push_queue.delete') + snackbar 'Couldn't delete. Please try again.' Because the server row still exists, the next refresh/realtime re-adds it.

flatCases.title: Discard of a seed/fresh-scan row with no __row_id is local-only
flatCases.preconditions: A seed/local sale entry not backed by a Supabase row (no __row_id).
steps: Open such a row, tap Delete, confirm.
flatCases.expected: onDiscard drops it locally and the sheet closes; because rowId is empty, NO Supabase delete runs and no 'Deleted.' DB op occurs.

flatCases.title: ANDROID ONLY: scanning a document inserts scan_jobs and raises the Processing badge
flatCases.preconditions: Android device, signed in, Queue open on the relevant tab.
steps: Tap the capture nav, pick Sale or Purchase, complete an ML Kit scan.
Observe the Processing tile/badge and timer ring.
flatCases.expected: ScanJobsService.startScan inserts a scan_jobs {type} row, returns its id (used as parser job_id), optimistically adds locally (deduped vs echo). The QueueLoadingTile shows count=1 for the active type with a timer ring from oldestStartFor.

flatCases.title: WEB/iOS: document scanning is unavailable and shows the not-supported message
flatCases.preconditions: Web session (or iOS), signed in.
steps: Tap the capture / add nav and choose a type.
flatCases.expected: A snackbar 'Document scanning is only available on Android.' is shown; no scan_jobs row is created. Web is a view/push-only consumer of the queue.

flatCases.title: Cross-client scan badge: phone scan raises and drains the badge on an open web session
flatCases.preconditions: Same tenant on Android phone and web, both on Queue.
steps: Scan on the phone.
Watch the web Processing badge climb (+1) then drain (-1) when the parsing service finishes and deletes the scan_jobs row.
flatCases.expected: scan_jobs_live INSERT echo increments the badge on every client; when parsing deletes the row and inserts the push_queue row, the DELETE echo drains the badge everywhere and the new invoice appears in the queue.

flatCases.title: Scan badge: 300s max-age sweep expires a missed DELETE so the badge can't wedge
flatCases.preconditions: A scan_jobs row whose DELETE is never delivered (e.g. scanning device went offline before its invoice landed).
steps: Create a scan_jobs row, then prevent the matching DELETE/parse completion.
Wait >300 seconds and watch the badge.
