flatCases.expected: columnLabels.indexOf('closing_stock_amount') returns -1 -> sumColumnIndex=null -> footer falls back to static footerLeading and 'N rows' (countUnit 'rows'), NO Σ total displayed. This confirms tight, fragile backend↔app coupling on the exact header literal.

flatCases.title: en-IN grouped / quoted numeric cells parse correctly into the Σ
flatCases.preconditions: CSV contains values like "1,36,433" (quoted, grouped).
steps: Open a report whose closing_stock_amount values are en-IN grouped (e.g. 1,36,433).
Verify the Σ against the un-grouped sum.
flatCases.expected: _cellToNum strips all but [0-9.\-] so "1,36,433" -> 136433; non-numeric/blank cells -> 0. Σ equals the sum of the de-grouped integers.

flatCases.title: Items with no purchase history emit blank closing_stock_amount and understate Σ
flatCases.preconditions: Client Supabase has at least one stock item with closing_qty>0 but no purchase voucher (purchaseRateRaw null).
steps: Open R7 (full portfolio) for a company having such items.
Locate the no-purchase-history item row; note its closing_stock_amount cell.
Compare the headline Σ to a manual valuation that values those items by some non-zero rate.
flatCases.expected: closing_stock_amount = closing_qty * purchaseRate; with purchaseRate null the cell is blank, _cellToNum('')=0, so the item contributes ₹0 to the Σ. The displayed closing-stock value silently UNDERSTATES true stock value. Flag as a data-integrity defect.

flatCases.title: Σ of pre-rounded integers can drift from a true rupee total
flatCases.preconditions: CSV closing_stock_amount values are Math.round + toLocaleString('en-IN') (paise dropped per row).
steps: Open a report with many rows whose true amounts have paise.
Compare the app Σ to a server-authoritative full-precision sum (compute from raw Supabase data).
flatCases.expected: Because per-row values are rounded server-side before the app sums them, the Σ can differ from a true full-precision total by a few rupees. Acceptable cosmetically but document the drift.

flatCases.title: Network down: report tap surfaces a snackbar and clears the spinner
flatCases.preconditions: Signed in. Device offline / backend unreachable (airplane mode or block the host).
steps: Tap any report row.
Wait for the request to fail.
Observe the row spinner and any snackbar.
flatCases.expected: client.get throws (SocketException etc.); _openReport catch clears _loadingCategoryKey and shows snackbar 'Failed to load report: <exception>'. The sheet does NOT open. On mobile, nothing is written to disk (write only happens after a 200), so no poisoned cache. ApiClient.reportFailure also logs to Sentry.

flatCases.title: 401 Unauthorized (x-api-key mismatch or API_KEY_CLIENT unset) -> 'Unauthorized' snackbar
flatCases.preconditions: Backend deployed with API_KEY_CLIENT unset OR app Config.mrpApiKey not matching backend API_KEY_CLIENT.
steps: Tap any report row.
Observe the snackbar.
flatCases.expected: Backend requireClientApiKey rejects -> 401. getRaw maps 401 to Exception('Unauthorized'); snackbar reads 'Failed to load report: Exception: Unauthorized'. Reports are completely unusable. Verify this is independent of API_KEY used by other endpoints (a deploy setting API_KEY but forgetting API_KEY_CLIENT breaks ALL reports while the rest of the app works).

flatCases.title: 404 Company not found (name drift / wrong DB) -> 'Request failed: 404'
flatCases.preconditions: Client Supabase has NO companies row exactly matching 'K V ENTERPRISES' (e.g. casing/whitespace differs, or pointing at a DB without that company).
steps: Tap any report row.
Observe the snackbar.
flatCases.expected: resolveCompanyLookup .eq('name','K V ENTERPRISES') returns 0 rows -> 404. Snackbar 'Failed to load report: Exception: Request failed: 404'. Because the company name is hardcoded in the app, any DB name drift makes ALL reports fail for everyone.

flatCases.title: 409 duplicate 'K V ENTERPRISES' rows -> every report tap fails (KNOWN ztugw P0)
flatCases.preconditions: Client/prod Supabase (ztugw) contains two or more companies rows named 'K V ENTERPRISES' (e.g. the orphan guid-null row).
steps: Tap any report row (any of R1-R7).
Observe the result for several reports.
flatCases.expected: resolveCompanyLookup .limit(2) sees >1 rows -> 409 'Multiple companies share this name...'. App shows generic 'Failed to load report: Exception: Request failed: 409' for EVERY report. This is the known production breakage; fix is removing the duplicate company row in ztugw. The user cannot distinguish this from the not-yet-synced 409.

flatCases.title: 409 company not yet synced (null last_synced_at) -> same generic 409 snackbar
flatCases.preconditions: Single 'K V ENTERPRISES' company exists in client Supabase but its last_synced_at is null (freshly added, no successful sync).
steps: Tap any report row.
Observe the snackbar.
flatCases.expected: resolveCompanyLookup defaults requireSuccessfulSync=true here -> 409 'Company has not completed a successful sync yet'. App shows 'Failed to load report: Exception: Request failed: 409' — INDISTINGUISHABLE from the duplicate-company 409. Reports become available only after a full sync lands.

flatCases.title: 500 server/Supabase failure -> 'Request failed: 500' snackbar
flatCases.preconditions: Force a server error: e.g. client Supabase unreachable, or an invalid format value reaching the handler (parseInventoryResponseFormat throws inside try -> caught as 500).
steps: Trigger a backend 500 (block reorderSupabase, or via a tampered request sending an invalid format).
Tap a report (or replay the tampered request).
Observe.
flatCases.expected: Backend catch returns 500 {error: message}. App shows 'Failed to load report: Exception: Request failed: 500'. Note a bad format yields 500 (not 400) by design. Sentry captures the failure with request_id/status/body.

flatCases.title: 400 invalid reportKey (not reachable from app UI) returns the keys list
flatCases.preconditions: Ability to hit the endpoint with a bad reportKey directly (curl/proxy) — the app only ever sends valid R1-R7.
steps: Send GET /api/sync/reorder-levels/NOTAKEY?company_name=K V ENTERPRISES&format=csv with valid x-api-key.
Observe the response.
flatCases.expected: normalizeInventoryReportKey returns null -> HTTP 400 with body listing allowed keys (R1/act_now ... R7/full_portfolio_health). Confirms the app's 7 seed reportIds are all valid and this branch is not user-reachable.

flatCases.title: Request timeout / slow backend: getRaw has no explicit timeout
flatCases.preconditions: Backend that stalls the response (e.g. throttle the connection or a sleeping proxy).
steps: Tap a report row.
Observe the row spinner while the request hangs.
Eventually let the socket time out at the OS/http layer.
flatCases.expected: getRaw issues a plain client.get with no .timeout(); the row spinner stays until the underlying http client/OS aborts the socket, then the catch shows 'Failed to load report: <exception>'. There is no app-level timeout countdown for reports (unlike the 300s parsing call). Note as a UX gap.

flatCases.title: Malformed/non-CSV 200 body surfaces a parse-failure snackbar
flatCases.preconditions: Backend/mock returns 200 with a body that breaks CsvToListConverter or a downstream parse.
steps: Force a 200 with malformed CSV (e.g. via proxy injecting garbage).
Tap the report.
Observe.
flatCases.expected: If parsing throws, the catch clears the spinner and shows 'Failed to load report: <exception>'. On mobile, note that the malformed body was already written to disk BEFORE parsing (write happens right after fetch on cache-miss) — so a subsequent re-tap will re-read the poisoned cache. Flag this caching-of-bad-body risk.

flatCases.title: Mobile poisoned-cache persistence: bad CSV stays cached after a parse error
flatCases.preconditions: Android. Force a 200 with a body that writes to disk but fails to parse/render usefully (see previous case).
steps: Tap a report; the bad body is written to /reports/<id>.csv and rendering fails or shows garbage.
Restore a healthy backend.
Re-tap the same report.
flatCases.expected: Because the file already exists, the cache-hit branch reads the stale/poisoned disk file and never refetches — the report stays broken until app data/cache is cleared. Confirms there is no TTL/invalidation and bad bodies are persisted.

flatCases.title: Mobile stale cache: data changes in Supabase but report shows old numbers
flatCases.preconditions: Android. A report (e.g. R1) already cached on disk. You can change underlying stock/voucher data in client Supabase (or run a fresh Tally sync).
steps: Open R1 on mobile (caches it).
Change the underlying data so the report should differ (e.g. add stock, complete a new sync).
Re-open R1 on mobile.
flatCases.expected: The mobile report still shows the OLD cached numbers (no TTL, no refresh, no invalidation), yet the footer labels it 'Live data'. This is a correctness/trust issue — the only way to refresh is clearing app data. Document as a P1 staleness defect.

flatCases.title: Mobile vs Web divergence: same user, same time, different numbers
flatCases.preconditions: Same account on Android (with a cached report) and on web. Underlying data changed since the mobile cache was written.
steps: On mobile open R7 (cached, stale).
On web open R7 (always refetch, fresh).
Compare the Σ and rows side by side.
flatCases.expected: Web shows fresh values; mobile shows the frozen cached snapshot. The identical report displays different totals on the two platforms simultaneously. Confirms web-refetch vs mobile-cache platform difference.

flatCases.title: PRIVACY: second user on same device sees first user's cached report
flatCases.preconditions: Android shared device. User A signs in and opens a report (caches /reports/<id>.csv).
steps: User A opens R3 (caches it), then signs out.
User B signs in on the same device.
User B opens R3.
flatCases.expected: Sign-out only clears the in-memory stock/customers/vendors caches, NOT the /reports/*.csv files. The cache-hit branch serves User A's inventory/value report to User B with no refetch. This is a cross-user data-leak / privacy defect — cached reports must be cleared on sign-out.

flatCases.title: Cache not cleared on sign-out (verify files persist)
flatCases.preconditions: Android. At least one report cached to /reports/.
steps: Open a report (caches it).
Sign out of the app.
Inspect <appDocs>/reports/ via file explorer/adb.
flatCases.expected: The /reports/<id>.csv file(s) still exist after sign-out (sign-out clears only in-memory caches). Confirms the missing-cleanup behavior underlying the privacy and staleness risks.

flatCases.title: Silent wrong-DB fallback: client env unset serves TESTING (yynuu) numbers
flatCases.preconditions: Backend deployed with SUPABASE_URL_Client / SUPABASE_SERVICE_KEY_CLIENT UNSET (so reorderSupabase falls back to the shared testing project).
steps: Tap a report.
Compare the returned numbers to the known client/prod (ztugw) values vs testing (yynuu) values.
flatCases.expected: With the client env unset, reorderSupabase silently falls back to the shared/testing Supabase with NO error. Reports return TESTING-project numbers to a production user (cross-tenant data exposure) with zero signal. Flag as a P0 config/data-integrity risk; mitigation is requiring the client env or failing loudly.

flatCases.title: API-key coupling: API_KEY set but API_KEY_CLIENT forgotten breaks only Reports
flatCases.preconditions: Backend deploy where API_KEY (used by every other endpoint) is set correctly but API_KEY_CLIENT is missing/wrong.
steps: Exercise a normal flow (e.g. push-queue activate) and confirm it works.
Then tap a report.
flatCases.expected: All non-report flows work, but every report tap returns 401 ('Unauthorized' snackbar) because reorder-levels uses its OWN key pair. Confirms the independent-key coupling is easy to miss in a deploy; add to deploy checklist.

flatCases.title: Concurrency: phone runs a Tally sync while web has the report open
flatCases.preconditions: Web has a report sheet open. A new sync/data change occurs server-side (no realtime channel exists for this domain).
steps: Open R1 on web (sheet showing).
Trigger a sync/data change that alters R1's underlying data.
Watch the open web sheet, then close and re-open R1 on web.
flatCases.expected: The open sheet does NOT live-update (Reports use no realtime channels — it is a one-shot GET). Closing and re-tapping on web refetches and shows the new numbers. On mobile, re-tap would still show the stale cache. Confirms no realtime coupling for this domain.

flatCases.title: Concurrency: rapid double-tap / tapping a second report while one is loading
flatCases.preconditions: Backend slightly slow so the spinner is visible.
steps: Tap report A; while its spinner is showing, tap report B.
Observe the spinners and which sheet opens.
flatCases.expected: _loadingCategoryKey is a single value, so the spinner moves to the most recently tapped row. Both in-flight requests complete; each opens its own bottom sheet in turn (modal stacking). No crash and the correct CSV maps to the correct sheet (each call captures its own category). Verify no cross-wiring of A's data into B's sheet.

flatCases.title: Concurrency: report opened mid-sync returns a partially-updated snapshot
flatCases.preconditions: A sync is actively writing vouchers/stock to client Supabase while the report query runs.
steps: Begin a server-side sync that mutates vouchers/voucher_items/stock_items.
During the write window, open R7 on web.
Inspect the totals for internal consistency.
flatCases.expected: The report reflects whatever rows are committed at query time (paginated reads via fetchAllPages are not a single snapshot); numbers may be transiently inconsistent but the request still returns 200 and renders. No crash; re-open after sync completes yields the final figures.

flatCases.title: WEB: 1.4x text scaling and desktop side-rail do not break the report sheet
flatCases.preconditions: Web build. Test at a wide (>=900px) and a narrow (<900px) viewport.
steps: Load the app on web at >=900px width: confirm side-rail nav.
Open a report and inspect layout/legibility (1.4x text scaling).
Shrink below 900px: confirm bottom-nav and re-open the report.
flatCases.expected: At >=900px the side-rail is shown; below 900px the bottom-nav. In both, the report bottom sheet renders at heightFactor 0.92 with 1.4x-scaled text that remains legible and non-overflowing. The Σ footer, search, and Close button all function.

flatCases.title: MOBILE: report sheet renders at 0.92 height and scrolls horizontally
flatCases.preconditions: Android phone, a report opened.
steps: Open a wide report (many columns) on a phone.
Scroll the spreadsheet horizontally and vertically.
Confirm the footer Σ and Share/Close controls.
flatCases.expected: Sheet opens at 92% screen height; columns (width 42 / 240 / 96...) are horizontally scrollable; rows scroll vertically. Footer shows Σ and 'Items' count; Share and Close are present and work.

flatCases.title: WEB attempts no path_provider / disk access for reports
flatCases.preconditions: Web build with console open.
steps: Open a report on web.
Watch the browser console for MissingPluginException / path_provider errors.
flatCases.expected: On web the kIsWeb branch fetches directly and never calls _cacheFile/getApplicationDocumentsDirectory, so there is no path_provider invocation and no MissingPluginException. No on-disk caching occurs.

flatCases.title: reportId==null seed branch is dead code with current seed data
flatCases.preconditions: Source review / a build where a seed category temporarily has reportId=null.
steps: Confirm all 7 seedReportCategories have non-null reportId (R1-R7).
(Optional) temporarily set one reportId=null in a debug build and tap it.
flatCases.expected: With current seed data the else-branch (static columnLabels/category.rows/'Σ footerSum') is never reached — confirmed dead code. If forced via reportId=null, it renders the local static columns with no network call; verify it does not crash.

flatCases.title: Authorization Bearer is attached but ignored; report works while signed in
flatCases.preconditions: Signed in (Firebase JWT available).
steps: Capture the outgoing report GET headers.
Confirm Authorization Bearer <jwt> is present alongside x-api-key.
Confirm the request still succeeds purely on the x-api-key.
flatCases.expected: ApiClient attaches the Firebase Bearer JWT, but requireClientApiKey only checks x-api-key. The report returns 200 regardless of JWT validity. (Optional: an expired/absent JWT does not affect the report response.)

flatCases.title: Hardcoded company/report params: no other tenant or report can be viewed
flatCases.preconditions: App as shipped (company_name='K V ENTERPRISES', reportIds R1-R7 baked in).
steps: Inspect the outgoing query for every report tap.
Confirm company_name is always 'K V ENTERPRISES' and format always 'csv'.
Confirm there is no UI to choose a different company or pass company_guid/company_id.
flatCases.expected: Every request hard-codes company_name='K V ENTERPRISES' and format=csv. No other tenant is reachable from the app; any DB-side name drift (case/whitespace) breaks all reports. Confirms the single-tenant hardcoding limitation.

flatCases.title: User cannot distinguish 404 vs the two 409s vs 500 from the snackbar
flatCases.preconditions: Ability to reproduce a 404, a duplicate-company 409, a not-synced 409, and a 500 (separately).
steps: Reproduce each error condition in turn and tap a report.
Record the exact snackbar text for each.
flatCases.expected: 404/409/500 all surface as 'Failed to load report: Exception: Request failed: <code>' and 401 as 'Exception: Unauthorized'. The two distinct 409 causes (duplicate company vs not-yet-synced) are indistinguishable to the user. Recommend differentiated messaging; meanwhile Sentry body carries the real reason.

flatCases.title: Failures are reported to Sentry with request_id/endpoint/status correlation
flatCases.preconditions: Sentry DSN configured on app and backend.
steps: Trigger a report failure (e.g. 409 or network error).
In Sentry, find the corresponding event.
flatCases.expected: ApiClient.reportFailure captures an event tagged with request_id, endpoint '/api/sync/reorder-levels/<id>', status, and response body. The x-request-id matches between the app event and the backend event (cross-correlated). Confirms observability for report failures.

flatCases.title: GST SALE 6-month / purchase 1-month windows shape the report correctly
flatCases.preconditions: Client Supabase has sales older than 6 months, sales within 6 months, purchases older than 1 month, and purchases within 1 month, plus some is_cancelled=true vouchers.
steps: Open R1/R4 (which use sale_6m and purchase_1m windows).
Cross-check that only GST SALE vouchers in the last 6 calendar months and purchases in the last 1 calendar month (excluding cancelled and order-type) contributed.
flatCases.expected: Server-side: sales filtered to voucher_type='GST SALE', is_cancelled=false, date within last 6 calendar months; purchases to is_cancelled=false within last 1 calendar month and isPurchaseVoucherType (excludes 'order'). Cancelled/out-of-window vouchers are excluded from the report aggregates. Verify the rendered figures reflect those windows.

flatCases.title: Spinner clears even when the bottom sheet is dismissed immediately
flatCases.preconditions: A report loads successfully.
steps: Tap a report, let it open, then swipe-down/Close the sheet quickly.
Re-inspect the list row.
flatCases.expected: _loadingCategoryKey is set to null before showModalBottomSheet, so the row spinner is already cleared when the sheet opens; dismissing the sheet returns to a clean list with no stuck spinner. Re-tapping works again.

flatCases.title: Navigating away mid-load does not crash (mounted guard)
flatCases.preconditions: Backend slow enough that the request is in flight.
steps: Tap a report; while loading, navigate away from the Report screen (switch tab/nav).
Let the request complete or fail.
flatCases.expected: The mounted checks guard setState and ScaffoldMessenger; if the widget is unmounted when the response/exception arrives, no setState-after-dispose exception is thrown and no sheet/snackbar is forced onto a disposed context.

flatCases.title: Sign-in loads all three master caches (stock + customers + vendors)
flatCases.preconditions: Logged out. Test Supabase project (yynuu) has stock_items (>0 rows), ledgers with Sundry Debtors and Sundry Creditors rows. Network up.
steps: Launch the app and complete phone-number OTP login (+91).
Open any PENDING voucher in the queue and tap Edit to enter edit mode.
Tap the party name to open the party picker.
Close it, tap Add Item to open the stock picker, and toggle the 'All items' switch ON.
flatCases.expected: Party picker lists customers (sale) / vendors (purchase); stock picker 'All items' view lists catalog stock with rates. None of the lists is empty and no 'download failed' snackbar appears.

flatCases.title: Web cold-start / page refresh restores session and refetches caches
flatCases.preconditions: Already signed in on web.
steps: With the app open and signed in, press browser Refresh (F5).
Wait for the splash to resolve to the shell.
Open a pending voucher, enter edit mode, and open the stock 'All items' picker and the party picker.
flatCases.expected: Session is restored via authStateChanges (no re-login prompt) and all three caches are re-fetched fresh; pickers are populated after a brief load.

flatCases.title: uid guard suppresses redundant cache reload on token refresh / same-user re-emit
flatCases.preconditions: Signed in. Ability to observe network (web devtools Network tab or proxy).
steps: Sign in and let caches load; note the stock_items/ledgers requests in the network log.
Leave the app idle long enough for a Firebase token refresh, or trigger any authStateChanges re-emit for the same user.
Inspect the network log for new stock_items / ledgers fetches.
flatCases.expected: No second round of stock_items/ledgers fetches fires for the same uid (lastUid guard); caches stay populated with no flicker.

flatCases.title: Sign-out clears all caches (no stale master data left in memory)
flatCases.preconditions: Signed in with populated caches.
steps: From Profile, sign out.
Sign back in as the SAME user but immediately (before fetch completes) open a voucher and inspect pickers, then again after fetch completes.
flatCases.expected: On sign-out caches are emptied (items=[]); after re-login they repopulate. No party/stock rows from the previous session persist before the new fetch lands.

flatCases.title: User-switch isolation: sign out as A, sign in as B shows only B-scoped masters
flatCases.preconditions: Two accounts A and B. (Note: in single-project-per-client model both may resolve to the same Supabase project; verify no in-memory leakage regardless.)
steps: Sign in as user A, load caches, note a distinctive customer/stock row.
Sign out (caches cleared).
Sign in as user B and open the party + stock pickers.
flatCases.expected: Caches are cleared on A's sign-out and repopulated from B's session; no A-only in-memory rows appear before B's fetch resolves. RLS/anon scoping returns only data the active session is entitled to.

flatCases.title: Stock catalog pagination loads the full ~13k item set (beyond 1000)
flatCases.preconditions: stock_items has well over 1000 rows (e.g. ~13k).
steps: Sign in and wait for stock load to finish.
Open a pending voucher, Edit, Add Item, toggle 'All items' ON.
Read the 'count :' value, then search for a stock item known to sort late alphabetically (e.g. starting with 'Z').
flatCases.expected: Count reflects the full catalog (~13k, not capped at 1000); the late-alphabetical item is present, proving .range() pagination looped past the first 1000-row page.

flatCases.title: Stock pagination boundary at an exact 1000-row multiple
flatCases.preconditions: stock_items row count is an exact multiple of 1000 (e.g. exactly 2000) in a test project.
steps: Sign in and let stock load.
Open the 'All items' stock picker and read 'count :'.
flatCases.expected: All rows are present (e.g. 2000) and the fetch loop terminates cleanly without hanging or duplicating the last page (a full final page triggers one extra empty/short page that ends the loop).

flatCases.title: Empty stock_items / RLS misconfig returns 200 [] -> silently empty stock cache
flatCases.preconditions: Point the app at a project where the anon/publishable key or RLS yields zero stock_items rows (200 with empty array, not an error).
steps: Sign in and wait for cache load.
Open a pending voucher, Edit, Add Item, toggle 'All items' ON.
Observe the stock list and whether any error/snackbar appeared.
flatCases.expected: Stock picker is empty with NO 'download failed' snackbar and NO Sentry error (200 [] is not an exception). Confirms the silent-empty-cache risk where unitFor/partCodeFor will return '' -> 'NOS' default.

flatCases.title: Network down during stock fetch -> 'download failed' snackbar shown
flatCases.preconditions: Ability to disable network right at sign-in (airplane mode / block Supabase host).
steps: Disable network, then sign in (or trigger authStateChanges with network off).
Observe the app's scaffold for a snackbar.
Re-enable network and sign out/in to recover.
flatCases.expected: StockItemsCache.fetch throws, reportHandledError('supabase.stock_items.fetch') fires, and a 'download failed ...' snackbar is shown (StockItemsCache has scaffoldKey wired). Pickers are empty until a successful re-fetch.

flatCases.title: Partial stock pagination failure mid-loop leaves cache empty (no partial commit)
flatCases.preconditions: Ability to fail the 2nd/3rd .range() page (e.g. kill network after first page returns).
steps: Sign in; allow the first 1000-row page to load, then drop the network so a subsequent page request fails.
Open the 'All items' stock picker.
flatCases.expected: Because items is only assigned after the full loop succeeds, a mid-loop failure leaves the cache at its prior value (empty on first load); a 'download failed' snackbar appears. No partial 1000-row set is silently presented as complete.

flatCases.title: Customer ledger > 1000 Sundry Debtors is silently truncated (no pagination)
flatCases.preconditions: ledgers has > 1000 rows with group_name='Sundry Debtors' in the active project.
steps: Sign in and let CustomersCache load.
Open a pending SALE voucher, Edit, tap the party name to open the customer picker.
Search for a customer known to exist but sorted/positioned beyond the 1000th Sundry Debtor row.
flatCases.expected: DEFECT TO CONFIRM: the customer is missing because CustomersCache.fetch has no .range() and PostgREST caps the response at 1000 rows, so the party is unselectable (mis-parsed party cannot be fixed -> push may be blocked or pushed under wrong ledger).

flatCases.title: Vendor ledger > 1000 Sundry Creditors is silently truncated (no pagination)
flatCases.preconditions: ledgers has > 1000 rows with group_name='Sundry Creditors'.
steps: Sign in and let VendorsCache load.
Open a pending PURCHASE voucher, Edit, tap the party name to open the vendor picker.
Search for a vendor positioned beyond the 1000th Sundry Creditor row.
flatCases.expected: DEFECT TO CONFIRM: the vendor is absent (1000-row cap, no pagination) and cannot be selected for a mis-parsed purchase party.

flatCases.title: Customer fetch failure produces NO visible snackbar (scaffoldKey never wired)
flatCases.preconditions: Ability to make the ledgers Sundry Debtors fetch throw (network off at sign-in / block host). Sentry observable.
steps: Disable network and sign in so CustomersCache.fetch throws.
Watch the app scaffold for any snackbar.
Check the Sentry dashboard for a 'supabase.customers.fetch' event.
flatCases.expected: DEFECT TO CONFIRM: no user-visible snackbar appears (CustomersCache.scaffoldKey is never assigned in main.dart), so the failure is silent client-side; only a Sentry reportHandledError event records it. Party picker is empty.

flatCases.title: Vendor fetch failure produces NO visible snackbar (scaffoldKey never wired)
flatCases.preconditions: Ability to make the ledgers Sundry Creditors fetch throw. Sentry observable.
steps: Disable network and sign in so VendorsCache.fetch throws.
Watch for a snackbar; then check Sentry for 'supabase.vendors.fetch'.
flatCases.expected: DEFECT TO CONFIRM: no snackbar (VendorsCache.scaffoldKey never wired); only Sentry records it. Vendor picker is empty with no on-screen warning.

flatCases.title: RLS/anon-key misconfig returns 200 [] for ledgers -> empty party picker, no error
flatCases.preconditions: App pointed at a project where the anon/publishable key or RLS yields zero ledgers rows for the group filters (200 empty array).
steps: Sign in and wait.
Open a pending sale voucher, Edit, tap party name.
Repeat on a purchase voucher for vendors.
flatCases.expected: Both party pickers are empty with no exception, no snackbar, no Sentry event (mirrors the parsing service_role-key memory note). User cannot reselect a party and gets no indication why.

flatCases.title: Open customer picker on a pending SALE voucher lists Sundry Debtors
flatCases.preconditions: Signed in, caches loaded, a PENDING sale voucher in queue.
steps: Open the sale voucher and tap Edit.
Tap the party name (shows dropdown caret) to open _CustomerPickerSheet.
Type part of a known customer name.
flatCases.expected: Picker opens with the customer list (Sundry Debtors); case-insensitive name.contains filtering narrows results per keystroke; tapping a row sets the editable party name.

flatCases.title: Open vendor picker on a pending PURCHASE voucher lists Sundry Creditors
flatCases.preconditions: Signed in, caches loaded, a PENDING purchase voucher in queue.
steps: Open the purchase voucher and tap Edit.
Tap the party name to open the picker (search hint reads 'Search vendors…').
Filter and select a vendor.
flatCases.expected: Picker lists vendors (Sundry Creditors); selecting one updates the editable party name.

flatCases.title: Party picker tap while ledger cache is still loading shows 'still downloading' and does not open
flatCases.preconditions: Sign-in with a slow/throttled connection so CustomersCache.isLoading is still true when the voucher is opened.
steps: Immediately after login, open a pending sale voucher and tap Edit.
Tap the party name while the customer cache is still loading.
flatCases.expected: A snackbar 'Please wait, customer list is still downloading…' appears and the picker does NOT open (guard at the party tap). Same with 'vendor list' wording on a purchase voucher.

flatCases.title: Party name is NOT editable when voucher is not in edit mode or not pending
flatCases.preconditions: A voucher in view mode (not editing) and/or a non-pending (push_now/failed/pushed) voucher.
steps: Open a pending voucher WITHOUT tapping Edit and tap the party name.
Open a non-pending voucher, tap Edit if allowed, and try tapping the party name.
flatCases.expected: In view mode the party name is plain text (no dropdown caret, tap does nothing). Edit affordance only appears when _isEditing && !_loading, so the party picker cannot be opened outside an editable pending voucher.

flatCases.title: Empty customer cache blocks fixing a mis-parsed party (push stays blocked)
flatCases.preconditions: CustomersCache empty (RLS 200 [] or fetch failed). A pending sale voucher whose parsed party is wrong.
steps: Open the sale voucher, Edit, tap the party name.
Observe the empty picker; attempt to change party to the correct one.
Attempt to push the voucher.
flatCases.expected: Picker is empty so the correct customer cannot be selected; combined with the party-changed/items-changed push guard, the voucher either cannot be corrected or risks being pushed under the wrong ledger. Confirms the data-integrity risk of silent empty caches.

flatCases.title: Stock picker defaults to party-history view and toggles to full catalog
flatCases.preconditions: Signed in, caches loaded, a pending sale voucher with a party that has prior voucher_items.
steps: Open the sale voucher, Edit, tap Add Item.
Observe the initial list (All items switch OFF = party-specific history).
Toggle 'All items' ON and observe the list change to the full catalog.
flatCases.expected: Default view shows party-specific items (source same_party, last rates); toggling 'All items' switches to the cached catalog. The 'count :' header updates with each view/filter.

flatCases.title: Stock picker keyboard navigation (Down/Up/Enter) selects highlighted row
flatCases.preconditions: On web/desktop with a physical keyboard. Stock picker open with a multi-row filtered list.
steps: Open the stock picker; type a query that returns several rows.
Press ArrowDown several times and watch the highlight + auto-scroll (ensureVisible).
Press ArrowUp once, then press Enter.
flatCases.expected: Highlight moves and the row scrolls into view (alignment 0.5); the search field keeps focus; Enter pops the currently highlighted item and adds it as a line. Arrow/Enter keys do not move the text cursor or submit the field.

flatCases.title: Stock picker is touch-only on mobile (no hardware keyboard nav)
flatCases.preconditions: On Android phone. Stock picker open.
steps: Type a query using the on-screen keyboard.
Scroll the list by touch and tap a row.
flatCases.expected: List filters and a tapped row is selected/added. No arrow-key highlight affordance is needed; selection works purely by touch.

flatCases.title: Stock picker search matches by Part No. (partCode) as well as name
flatCases.preconditions: Catalog has items with non-empty part_code values.
steps: Open the 'All items' stock picker.
Type a substring of a known Part No. (not present in the item name).
flatCases.expected: Items whose partCode contains the query are returned (filter checks name OR partCode, case-insensitive); the partCode is shown under the item name.

flatCases.title: Add item from party-history carries that party's latest rate and discount onto the line
flatCases.preconditions: A pending sale voucher whose party has at least two historical vouchers for the same stock item at different rates/discounts.
steps: Open the sale voucher, Edit, Add Item (party-history view, All items OFF).
Pick a stock item that the party bought/sold before.
Inspect the new line's rate, discount_pct, and computed amount.
flatCases.expected: The line is seeded with the most-recent historical rate and discount_pct for that party (amount = qty*rate - qty*rate*discount/100). Tester must confirm this is the intended price, since pushing surfaces an outdated price/discount directly into the invoice/ledger totals.
integration_points: Supabase: voucher_items + vouchers (inner join, latest-rate dedup)

flatCases.title: Party-history query error silently falls back to catalog rates (no snackbar, no Sentry)
flatCases.preconditions: Ability to make the voucher_items inner-join query throw (drop network just as the picker opens, or break the voucher_items->vouchers FK in a test project).
steps: Open a pending sale voucher with a party, Edit, Add Item to trigger _fetchPartyItems.
Force the query to fail.
Observe the list contents and whether any error surfaced.
flatCases.expected: DEFECT TO CONFIRM: the bare catch(_) swallows the error and the picker silently shows the full catalog cache instead of party history; no snackbar and no Sentry event. User may unknowingly add catalog rates instead of party-specific rates.

flatCases.title: Party with > 4000 voucher_items may surface a stale 'latest' rate (no server-side order)
flatCases.preconditions: A high-volume party with > 4000 voucher_items rows where the genuinely most-recent rate for some item differs from older ones.
steps: Open a pending voucher for that party, Edit, Add Item (party-history view).
Pick an item and compare its shown rate against the true most-recent voucher rate for that party in the database.
flatCases.expected: DEFECT TO CONFIRM: because the query uses .limit(4000) with no server-side .order(), the returned slice is arbitrary; the client-side date-desc dedup can miss the truly latest voucher and present an older rate, risking a wrong price pushed to Tally.

flatCases.title: Party with no prior history shows empty party view; catalog toggle still works
flatCases.preconditions: A pending voucher whose party has zero matching voucher_items (new customer/vendor).
steps: Open the voucher, Edit, Add Item (party-history view).
Observe the empty list, then toggle 'All items' ON.
flatCases.expected: Party-history view is empty (count : 0) but does not error; toggling to 'All items' shows the full catalog so the user can still add a line.

flatCases.title: Unit backfill: party-history item with no unit resolves to catalog base unit
flatCases.preconditions: A party-history item whose voucher_items.unit is empty but whose catalog stock_items.unit is set (e.g. 'Kgs').
steps: Open a pending voucher, Edit, Add Item (party-history).
Pick the item whose history unit is blank.
Inspect the line's unit field.
flatCases.expected: unitFor() backfills the catalog unit (e.g. 'Kgs') via case-insensitive name match, so the line carries the correct Tally base unit rather than defaulting to 'NOS'.

flatCases.title: Empty/stale cache forces unit to 'NOS' -> Tally rejects line on push
flatCases.preconditions: StockItemsCache empty (RLS 200 [] or stale) OR the picked item not present in cache. Target Tally stock master uses a non-NOS base unit (e.g. Kgs/Pcs).
steps: With an empty/stale stock cache, open a pending voucher, Edit, Add Item.
Add an item whose unit is unknown to the cache; confirm the line shows unit 'NOS'.
Push the voucher and observe the Tally push result over realtime (tally_response errors).
flatCases.expected: unitFor() returns '' so the line defaults to 'NOS'; on push Tally rejects the line because the stock master's base unit differs (e.g. Kgs). This money/line-integrity failure is invisible at add-time (no snackbar) and only surfaces as a push error.

flatCases.title: Interior-whitespace/punctuation name mismatch makes unitFor return '' -> 'NOS'
flatCases.preconditions: A stock item whose voucher_items name differs from the catalog name by interior whitespace or punctuation (e.g. double space vs single space).
steps: Open a pending voucher, Edit, Add Item from party-history for that item.
Inspect the resolved unit on the line.
flatCases.expected: DEFECT TO CONFIRM: unitFor/partCodeFor only match on trim().toLowerCase() equality (not interior-whitespace-normalized), so the lookup misses and unit falls back to 'NOS', producing a wrong-unit line that Tally may reject.

flatCases.title: partCode backfill on party-history items shows/searches catalog Part No.
flatCases.preconditions: A party-history item that also exists in the catalog with a non-empty part_code.
steps: Open the party-history stock picker for that party.
Locate the item and confirm its Part No. is displayed.
Search by that Part No.
flatCases.expected: Although voucher_items has no part_code, partCodeFor() pulls it from the catalog cache so the Part No. is shown and is searchable.

flatCases.title: Cache staleness: item synced by desktop AFTER sign-in is invisible until re-login
flatCases.preconditions: Signed in on the app. A desktop TallyBridge sync adds a NEW stock item (and a new ledger) AFTER the app's sign-in.
steps: Note that the app caches loaded at sign-in.
On a separate machine, run a desktop sync that inserts a new stock item and a new Sundry Debtor.
Without re-logging-in, open a pending voucher, Edit, open the stock 'All items' picker and the party picker and search for the new entries.
flatCases.expected: The new item/ledger are ABSENT (caches refresh only at sign-in; no realtime/polling). After signing out and back in (or a web refresh), they appear. Adding a not-yet-cached line resolves unit/partCode to '' -> 'NOS'.

flatCases.title: Concurrency: phone scan + desktop sync while web session open keeps web masters stale
flatCases.preconditions: Web app signed in with caches loaded. A phone scan and/or desktop sync introduces new masters.
steps: Keep the web app open and signed in.
On the phone, scan a new invoice (parsing inserts a push_queue row) and/or run a desktop sync that adds masters.
On web, open a voucher and check the stock/party pickers for the new masters without refreshing.
flatCases.expected: Web pickers do NOT reflect the newly added masters until a refresh/re-login (in-memory caches, no realtime). Note distinction: the scan badge/queue update via realtime, but masters do not.

flatCases.title: Concurrency: two clients load masters simultaneously without interference
flatCases.preconditions: Same account signed in on phone and web (or two web tabs).
steps: Sign in on both clients at roughly the same time.
Let both finish loading and open the stock/party pickers on each.
flatCases.expected: Each client loads its own independent in-memory caches from Supabase; no shared state or race causes one client's picker to be empty or to show the other's filter state.

flatCases.title: Open voucher before caches finish -> entering edit mode blocked with stock-loading snackbar
flatCases.preconditions: Throttled network so StockItemsCache.isLoading is still true shortly after sign-in.
steps: Immediately after login, open a pending voucher.
Tap Edit (which would seed the edit session / add-item path) while stock is still loading.
flatCases.expected: A snackbar 'Loading of stock items in process, please wait' appears and edit mode is NOT entered (guard at !_isEditing && StockItemsCache.isLoading), preventing add-item against an incomplete catalog.

flatCases.title: Web 1.4x text scaling enlarges picker sheet rows and reduces visible count
flatCases.preconditions: On web. Stock or party picker open with many rows.
steps: Open the stock picker on web and note row height / how many rows fit in the 0.72-height sheet.
Compare against the same picker on mobile (or a non-web build).
flatCases.expected: On web the app-wide TextScaler.linear(1.4) propagates into the modal sheet (it sits under the app MediaQuery), making rows taller and showing fewer rows per screen; layout remains usable (no clipping/overflow of names).

flatCases.title: Web has no on-disk master cache; mobile keeps in-memory caches across foreground
flatCases.preconditions: Web build (no path_provider).
steps: Sign in on web and load caches.
Refresh the page (F5) and observe network for a fresh stock_items/ledgers fetch.
Separately on mobile, background and foreground the app and check whether masters refetch.
flatCases.expected: Web has no on-disk caching, so a refresh re-emits authStateChanges and triggers a full refetch; mobile keeps the same in-memory caches across background/foreground (no refetch) until sign-out or an auth re-emit. Masters are never persisted to disk on either platform.

flatCases.title: Desktop-web (>900px) two-pane layout: pickers function alongside the side-rail/two-pane sheet
flatCases.preconditions: Web window wider than the 900px breakpoint.
steps: Widen the browser past 900px so the bottom-nav becomes a side-rail and the voucher opens as a two-pane image+summary sheet.
Open the stock and party pickers from within the two-pane voucher view.
flatCases.expected: Pickers open and select correctly within the desktop two-pane layout; selection updates the summary pane. No layout breakage from the wider breakpoint.

flatCases.title: Search performance: typing in the ~13k-item stock picker stays responsive (no debounce)
flatCases.preconditions: Full ~13k catalog loaded, 'All items' view, on a low-end web client.
steps: Open the 'All items' stock picker.
Type and delete characters quickly to trigger repeated full-scan filters.
flatCases.expected: Each keystroke runs a linear .contains scan over ~13k items inside setState (no debounce). Acceptable: no crash; observe whether perceptible jank occurs (logged as a perf note rather than a functional failure).

flatCases.title: Abandoned RPCs are not called; party history uses the voucher_items inner-join query
flatCases.preconditions: Network capture available (web devtools / proxy).
steps: Open a pending voucher, Edit, Add Item to trigger party-history load.
Inspect outgoing Supabase calls.
flatCases.expected: The app issues a voucher_items select with a vouchers!inner embed (filtered by party_name + voucher_type ilike), and does NOT call get_sale_items_for_party / get_purchase_items_for_party RPCs (those are abandoned because the sync leaves voucher_items.party_name null).

flatCases.title: Customer picker case-insensitive contains filter narrows results per keystroke
flatCases.preconditions: CustomersCache loaded with several similarly-named customers.
steps: Open the customer picker on a pending sale voucher.
Type a lowercase substring that matches part of an uppercase customer name.
flatCases.expected: Filtering is case-insensitive name.contains; matching rows shrink as the query lengthens; clearing the field (suffix clear button) restores the full list.

flatCases.title: Selecting a corrected party updates editable party name and feeds the push guard
flatCases.preconditions: A pending sale voucher with a mis-parsed but cache-present customer; the correct customer IS in the cache.
steps: Open the voucher, Edit, tap party name, select the correct customer.
Confirm the displayed party name updates.
Add/modify line items as required and push.
flatCases.expected: _editablePartyName updates to the selected customer; on push the narration becomes 'Replara AI' and the voucher is activated under the corrected ledger. If party changed but not all items changed, the push is correctly BLOCKED by the guard (verify the block message).

flatCases.title: unitFor/partCodeFor return '' for blank or unknown names (defensive default)
flatCases.preconditions: Caches loaded.
steps: Trigger an add-item path where the selected item's name is empty or not in the catalog (e.g. a party-history row with an empty stock_item_name, which is skipped, or a name absent from catalog).
Inspect the resolved unit/partCode.
flatCases.expected: unitFor/partCodeFor return '' for empty/unknown names (early-return on empty target); the add path then defaults unit to 'NOS' and partCode to ''. Rows with empty stock_item_name are skipped entirely in party-history dedup.

flatCases.title: Customer/Vendor caches truncated at 1000 give no on-screen indication of incompleteness
flatCases.preconditions: ledgers Sundry Debtors slightly over 1000 rows.
steps: Open the customer picker and read whether any 'more results' / truncation indicator exists.
Scroll to the end of the list.
flatCases.expected: DEFECT TO CONFIRM: exactly 1000 rows load with NO truncation warning or 'showing 1000 of N' hint, so the tester/user cannot tell the list is incomplete.

flatCases.title: Sign out mid-fetch then immediately sign in does not leave caches stuck loading
flatCases.preconditions: Slow network so a fetch is in flight when sign-out occurs.
steps: Sign in; while caches are loading (isLoading=true), sign out.
Immediately sign back in.
Open pickers and observe whether they load or appear permanently stuck.
flatCases.expected: clear() resets isLoading=false and a new fetch starts on the re-emitted sign-in; the in-flight prior fetch's finally also resets isLoading. Pickers ultimately populate and are not stuck behind a loading guard. (Watch for any race leaving stale items briefly.)

flatCases.title: Mobile: no master refetch on app foreground (masters only refresh on auth re-emit)
flatCases.preconditions: Android, signed in, caches loaded. A desktop sync adds a master while app is backgrounded.
steps: Background the app for a while; add a new stock item via desktop sync.
Foreground the app (without sign-out) and open the stock 'All items' picker.
flatCases.expected: The new item is NOT present on foreground because masters have no foreground-resync (that mechanism is scan_jobs only); masters refresh only when authStateChanges re-emits a different uid (sign-out/in). Confirms staleness behavior on mobile.

flatCases.title: Testing flavor build targets yynuu Supabase + 828 backend + testing Firebase
flatCases.preconditions: Source checkout; env/testing.json present; able to build with --flavor testing --dart-define-from-file=env/testing.json.
steps: Build the app with FLAVOR=testing and run it.
Sign in with a test phone number and complete OTP.
Open any screen that reads Supabase (queue/history) and one that calls the main backend (a report).
Inspect Sentry events / network logs to confirm hostnames.
flatCases.expected: Supabase requests go to yynuuysvjeipawzfbeme.supabase.co; main-backend calls go to tallybridge-backend-828647628834; Firebase auth uses tallybridge-testing-env-636d4. No cross-project leakage; data shown matches the testing project.

flatCases.title: Deployment flavor build targets ztugw Supabase + 822 backend
flatCases.preconditions: env/deployment.json present; build with --flavor deployment --dart-define-from-file=env/deployment.json.
steps: Build with FLAVOR=deployment and run.
Sign in and load queue, history, and a report.
Confirm endpoint hostnames via logs.
flatCases.expected: Supabase = ztugwhevemibdrzqafyw (client/prod); backend/activate/parse all on 822222628942; SUPABASE_ANON_KEY = sb_publishable_IRsM... Data reflects the ztugw project consistently.

flatCases.title: Bare build with no dart-define falls back to testing defaults
flatCases.preconditions: Build the app WITHOUT --dart-define-from-file (no env file).
steps: Run flutter build/run with no --dart-define args.
Launch and inspect resolved Config values (log Config.supabaseUrl, backendBaseUrl, sentryEnvironment).
Sign in and load data.
flatCases.expected: All Config.* resolve to the hard-wired testing defaults (yynuu Supabase, 828 backend, FLAVOR='testing', sentryDsn=''). App still runs; Sentry is a no-op because default DSN is empty.

flatCases.title: prod.json placeholder: real prod Firebase but TESTING Supabase/backend (wrong-env hazard)
flatCases.preconditions: env/prod.json as committed (_PROD_PENDING_CONFIRM). Do NOT ship to real users; verify in a controlled build.
steps: Inspect env/prod.json values.
Build with FLAVOR=prod and run in a sandbox.
Sign in with a real-prod phone account; create/read a push_queue row; load a report.
Confirm which Supabase project actually receives the writes.
flatCases.expected: DEFECT TO FLAG: FLAVOR=prod authenticates real users against aiaccountant-b60ed Firebase, but SUPABASE_URL points to yynuu (TESTING) and BACKEND_BASE_URL/PARSE point to the stale 366926737745 project. Real users would read/write TESTING data. Build must be blocked from release until prod targets are confirmed.

flatCases.title: Android Dart FLAVOR must match gradle --flavor or native logins break
flatCases.preconditions: Android device; ability to build with mismatched gradle --flavor vs Dart FLAVOR define.
steps: Build Android with gradle --flavor testing but Dart-define FLAVOR=deployment (intentional mismatch).
Install and attempt phone-OTP login.
Repeat with matching flavor + define as control.
flatCases.expected: With mismatch, native google-services.json (testing) and Dart FirebaseOptions (deployment) target different Firebase projects and Android login fails / OTP never verifies. With matched flavor+define, login succeeds. Confirms the firebase_options.dart warning.

flatCases.title: Web build selects web FirebaseOptions per flavor (ignores google-services.json)
flatCases.preconditions: Web build for each flavor.
steps: Build web with FLAVOR=testing and FLAVOR=deployment separately.
Sign in on each and observe Firebase project used (authDomain in network calls).
flatCases.expected: Web uses the _xxxWeb FirebaseOptions chosen by FLAVOR+kIsWeb; testing build hits testing Firebase, deployment hits deployment Firebase. No google-services.json involvement on web.

flatCases.title: All three flavors share one Sentry DSN, differentiated only by environment tag
flatCases.preconditions: Sentry project access; builds for testing and deployment.
steps: Run a testing build and trigger a handled error (e.g. force a backend 500).
Run a deployment build and trigger a similar error.
In Sentry, filter by the environment tag.
flatCases.expected: Both events land in the same Sentry project (DSN identical across env files); they are distinguishable only by environment=testing vs environment=deployment. No per-env project isolation.

flatCases.title: Web blocks http (mixed-content) targets; all shipped URLs are https
flatCases.preconditions: Web build served over https.
steps: Confirm all flavor URLs (supabase/backend/parse) are https (they are).
Temporarily configure a build with an http BACKEND_BASE_URL and attempt a report fetch on web.
Restore https and retry.
flatCases.expected: With https URLs all requests succeed. With an http target, the browser blocks the request as mixed content (web only); native mobile would still attempt it. Confirms web-specific transport constraint.

flatCases.title: Cold start signed-out shows LoginScreen
flatCases.preconditions: No persisted Firebase session (fresh install / signed out).
steps: Launch the app cold.
Observe initial route after splash.
flatCases.expected: authStateChanges emits no user -> LoginScreen is shown. No data caches loaded; no Supabase reads attempted as a user.

flatCases.title: Cold start with persisted session restores into AccountantShell
flatCases.preconditions: Previously signed in (persisted session exists).
steps: Launch the app cold.
Observe route after splash.
flatCases.expected: authStateChanges emits the persisted user -> AccountantShell; caches (stock/customers/vendors) load; no re-login required.

flatCases.title: Web refresh (F5) restores Firebase session via authStateChanges stream
flatCases.preconditions: Signed in on web.
steps: Sign in on the web app.
Press browser refresh / reload the tab.
Observe whether you stay signed in.
flatCases.expected: SplashScreen shows briefly (ConnectionState.waiting) then AccountantShell — session is restored because home gates on the authStateChanges() stream, not a one-time currentUser read. User is NOT bounced to login.

flatCases.title: SplashScreen shown while auth state is resolving
flatCases.preconditions: App launching with slow auth restore.
steps: Launch the app / refresh web with throttled network.
Observe the transient state before login or shell.
flatCases.expected: While StreamBuilder is in ConnectionState.waiting, SplashScreen is displayed (no flash of LoginScreen for an already-signed-in user).

flatCases.title: Phone OTP login happy path with +91 prefix
flatCases.preconditions: Valid Indian phone number with SMS access.
steps: Enter a 10-digit number on LoginScreen.
Tap continue; verifyPhoneNumber is called with '+91'+number.
Enter the received OTP on OtpScreen.
flatCases.expected: OTP verifies, FirebaseAuth signs in, app navigates to AccountantShell, and a JWT is obtainable via getIdToken(). Number is sent with hardcoded +91 country code.

flatCases.title: Phone number shorter/longer than 10 digits is rejected before send
flatCases.preconditions: On LoginScreen.
steps: Enter a 9-digit number and attempt continue.
Enter an 11-digit number and attempt continue.
Enter exactly 10 digits.
flatCases.expected: 9- and 11-digit inputs are blocked by the 10-digit guard (no verifyPhoneNumber call / SMS sent); only the 10-digit input proceeds.

flatCases.title: Wrong OTP code shows error and does not sign in
flatCases.preconditions: Reached OtpScreen with a real verificationId.
steps: Enter an incorrect 6-digit OTP.
Submit.
flatCases.expected: Firebase returns an invalid-code error; an error message is shown; user remains on OtpScreen, not signed in.

flatCases.title: Android SMS auto-retrieval auto-signs in (verificationCompleted)
flatCases.preconditions: Android device that supports SMS auto-retrieval; valid number.
steps: Initiate OTP login on Android.
Wait for the SMS to arrive without manually typing the code.
flatCases.expected: verificationCompleted fires and auto-signs the user in without manual OTP entry (Android-only convenience). On web/iOS this path does not trigger and manual entry is required.

flatCases.title: Sign-in warms StockItems/Customers/Vendors caches
flatCases.preconditions: Signed out; valid account with stock/ledger data in the active Supabase project.
steps: Sign in.
Open SALE stock picker, customer list, and vendor list shortly after.
flatCases.expected: _wireSessionAndSentryUser fetches StockItemsCache/CustomersCache/VendorsCache on the uid transition; pickers/lists populate from cache without per-open round trips.

flatCases.title: Sign-out clears all session caches
flatCases.preconditions: Signed in with caches loaded.
steps: Sign out.
(If possible) inspect that StockItems/Customers/Vendors caches are emptied.
Sign back in as a different user and confirm fresh data loads.
flatCases.expected: On sign-out the three caches clear; no stale data from the previous user leaks into the next session.

flatCases.title: Token refresh (same uid) does not redundantly reload caches
flatCases.preconditions: Signed in; leave app open long enough for an ID-token refresh.
steps: Stay signed in and idle until Firebase refreshes the ID token (authStateChanges may re-emit same uid).
Observe whether caches reload.
flatCases.expected: The uid guard detects the unchanged uid and skips a redundant cache reload; no flicker / duplicate fetch storms on token refresh.

flatCases.title: Sentry scope tagged with SentryUser(uid) on sign-in
flatCases.preconditions: Build with a non-empty SENTRY_DSN; signed out.
steps: Sign in.
Trigger a handled error (e.g. force a backend failure).
Inspect the Sentry event's user field.
flatCases.expected: The event carries SentryUser(id: uid) set during _wireSessionAndSentryUser, allowing per-user grouping.

flatCases.title: Sentry user cleared on sign-out
flatCases.preconditions: Build with DSN; signed in with Sentry user set.
steps: Sign out.
Trigger a handled error while signed out (if reachable).
Inspect the Sentry event's user field.
flatCases.expected: After sign-out the Sentry user scope is cleared so subsequent events are not attributed to the previous uid.

flatCases.title: Signed-in backend GET sends Bearer + x-api-key + x-request-id
flatCases.preconditions: Signed in; build with non-empty DSN to inspect breadcrumbs, or proxy the request.
steps: Trigger any ApiClient.get/post (e.g. open an image or report).
Capture the outgoing request headers via a proxy or Sentry breadcrumb.
flatCases.expected: Headers include Content-Type: application/json (get/post), x-api-key: Config.mrpApiKey, x-request-id: <hex-hex>, and Authorization: Bearer <getIdToken()>. Backend requireApiKey verifies the Bearer first and ignores x-api-key.

flatCases.title: Signed-out backend call falls back to x-api-key path
flatCases.preconditions: Signed out but a code path that still calls ApiClient (e.g. activate is API-key only).
steps: With no Firebase user, invoke an ApiClient call that does not require a Bearer (activate).
Capture headers.
flatCases.expected: No Authorization header is attached (token null); backend requireApiKey/requireClientApiKey matches x-api-key against API_KEY/API_KEY_CLIENT. Call succeeds purely on the shipped publishable key.

flatCases.title: Backend 401 surfaces as Exception('Unauthorized')
flatCases.preconditions: Ability to force a 401 (expired token or wrong key).
steps: Make an ApiClient.get/getRaw/getBytes call with an invalid/expired Bearer and a non-matching x-api-key.
Observe the thrown error and that a Sentry failure event is recorded.
flatCases.expected: reportFailure(status:401) fires, then the call throws Exception('Unauthorized'). Caller sees an auth error rather than parsing a body.

flatCases.title: Non-401 non-2xx (409/500) get/post is reported but error body decoded as success
flatCases.preconditions: Ability to force the backend to return a 409 or 500 with a JSON body from an ApiClient.get/post call.
steps: Trigger an ApiClient.get or post that returns HTTP 409/500 with a JSON error body.
Observe what the caller receives.
flatCases.expected: DEFECT TO FLAG: reportFailure logs to Sentry but the method then returns jsonDecode(res.body) (no throw for non-401). A 409/500 error JSON is handed to the caller as if it were valid data, masking the failure. getRaw/getBytes do throw on non-200, but get/post do not.

flatCases.title: Non-JSON error body in get/post throws FormatException
flatCases.preconditions: Force a backend response with a non-JSON body (e.g. an HTML 500 page) on a get/post route.
steps: Trigger a get/post that returns HTTP 500 with a plain-text/HTML body.
Observe behavior after reportFailure.
flatCases.expected: jsonDecode throws FormatException (since status != 401 and not parseable); caller gets a confusing FormatException instead of a clean error. Confirms inconsistent error handling.

flatCases.title: Offline / network down reports failure then rethrows
flatCases.preconditions: Signed in; ability to disable network.
steps: Turn off Wi-Fi/data.
Trigger an ApiClient call (report/image/activate).
flatCases.expected: The SocketException/timeout is caught, reportFailure(error) records a Sentry event tagged with the request_id and endpoint, then the error is rethrown to the caller. UI shows a network error, not silent success.

flatCases.title: No HTTP timeout: hung backend stalls the call indefinitely
flatCases.preconditions: Ability to point at a backend that accepts the connection but never responds (or sleep).
steps: Configure a slow/hung backend endpoint.
Trigger an ApiClient.get and an activate POST.
Wait several minutes.
flatCases.expected: DEFECT TO FLAG: Neither ApiClient nor the activate POST sets a timeout (default http.Client has none), so the call hangs indefinitely with no user feedback. (Contrast: parsing uploads in another domain do set 300s.)

flatCases.title: getRaw strips Content-Type and throws on any non-200
flatCases.preconditions: Reorder/report path uses getRaw.
steps: Trigger getRaw against an endpoint returning 200 then one returning 500.
Capture request headers and the thrown error.
flatCases.expected: Request omits Content-Type (kept x-api-key + Bearer). 200 returns the raw body; any non-200 calls reportFailure and throws (401 -> Unauthorized, else 'Request failed: <code>'). No silent decode.

flatCases.title: getBytes returns image bytes on 200 and throws on non-200
flatCases.preconditions: A push_queue row with a stored invoice image; signed in.
steps: Open the two-pane image viewer for a row that has an image.
Then attempt one for a row whose image is missing (force 404).
flatCases.expected: 200 returns the JPEG bytes and the image renders; 404/500 calls reportFailure and throws 'Request failed' (401 -> Unauthorized). No bytes returned on error.

flatCases.title: x-request-id is sent but never echoed/used by backend (correlation blind spot)
flatCases.preconditions: Backend deployed as-is (no Sentry, no x-request-id middleware).
steps: Trigger any ApiClient call and note the x-request-id sent.
Inspect the backend response headers and backend logs/Sentry for that id.
flatCases.expected: DEFECT TO FLAG: backend has no Sentry dependency and no x-request-id middleware; it never reads or echoes the header. The advertised app<->backend request_id correlation does not exist server-side. Response carries no x-request-id back.

flatCases.title: Firebase token expires mid-session -> Bearer routes 401, re-auth recovers
flatCases.preconditions: Signed in; ability to invalidate/expire the ID token (e.g. revoke session or wait past expiry without refresh).
steps: Force the current ID token to be invalid/expired.
Trigger a Bearer-authed call (image fetch).
Then let the app refresh the token (re-fetch getIdToken) and retry.
flatCases.expected: With an expired token the backend returns 401 ('Invalid or expired token') and the call throws Unauthorized. After a fresh getIdToken the retry succeeds. App should surface re-auth rather than crash.

flatCases.title: Activate happy path: payload narration overwritten then POST flips pending->push_now
flatCases.preconditions: A push_queue row with status='pending' and a valid voucher_payload; signed in.
steps: Open the voucher detail sheet for the pending row.
Tap Push.
Observe the Supabase update then the activate POST and resulting status.
flatCases.expected: voucher_detail_sheet first updates push_queue.voucher_payload (narration forced to the fixed _pushNarration, '__' keys stripped) for that id, then POSTs activate; backend flips status pending->push_now and returns 2xx. UI enters awaitingPushResult.

flatCases.title: Activate sends x-api-key only, NO Authorization Bearer
flatCases.preconditions: Signed in; proxy to inspect the activate request.
steps: Tap Push and capture the activate POST headers.
flatCases.expected: Headers are manual {Content-Type, x-api-key: Config.activateApiKey, x-request-id} with NO Bearer. Backend requireApiKey matches x-api-key==API_KEY via timingSafeEqual. (Unlike ApiClient.get which adds Bearer.)

flatCases.title: Activate 400 when job_id missing
flatCases.preconditions: Ability to send activate with an empty/missing job_id (e.g. corrupted row id).
steps: Trigger activate without job_id in the body.
flatCases.expected: Backend returns 400 'job_id required'; UI reports failure via ApiClient.reportFailure and does not enter awaitingPushResult.

flatCases.title: Activate 404 when job not found
flatCases.preconditions: A job_id that does not exist in push_queue.
steps: Tap Push on a row that was deleted server-side just before (or send a bogus job_id).
flatCases.expected: Backend returns 404 'job not found'; activate POST is reported to Sentry; UI shows push failure, no status change.

flatCases.title: Activate 409 when row is not in 'pending' status
flatCases.preconditions: A push_queue row whose status is already push_now/pushed/failed.
steps: Open the detail sheet for a non-pending row (or change status server-side then push).
Tap Push.
flatCases.expected: Backend returns 409 'must be pending (current status: X)'; push is rejected; no double-activation. UI surfaces the failure.

flatCases.title: Activate 409 when job belongs to a different company
flatCases.preconditions: Backend configured with company-identity check; a row whose company_id/guid/name mismatches the request.
steps: Trigger activate with a company identity that does not match the row.
Observe response.
flatCases.expected: Backend returns 409 'job does not belong to requested company'; the wrong-company voucher is NOT activated, preventing a cross-company push.

flatCases.title: Activate 401 on x-api-key mismatch
flatCases.preconditions: Build with an ACTIVATE_API_KEY that does not equal backend API_KEY.
steps: Tap Push.
Observe response.
flatCases.expected: Backend requireApiKey returns 401 Unauthorized (length/timingSafeEqual mismatch). Activate fails cleanly; payload was still mutated (see rollback case).

flatCases.title: Activate POST failure leaves payload narration mutated with status still pending (no rollback)
flatCases.preconditions: A pending row; force the activate POST to fail (network/401/409) AFTER the Supabase update succeeds.
steps: Open the detail sheet, tap Push.
Let the Supabase voucher_payload update succeed, then force the activate POST to fail.
Re-open the row and inspect voucher_payload/narration and status.
flatCases.expected: DEFECT TO FLAG: the row keeps the overwritten narration (_pushNarration) and status stays 'pending' with no rollback. The voucher payload is edited without a successful push, so a later push uses the forced narration even if the user never intended it.

flatCases.title: Signed-out client with shipped publishable key can call activate
flatCases.preconditions: Knowledge that ACTIVATE_API_KEY == shipped Supabase publishable key; ability to replay the activate request without a Firebase session.
steps: Capture a valid activate request.
Replay it with x-api-key but no Bearer (signed-out).
flatCases.expected: DEFECT TO FLAG: activate succeeds on API-key only because the backend API_KEY equals the publishable key compiled into the app. Anyone holding the shipped key can activate pushes without authenticating. Security risk to record.

flatCases.title: Activate terminal result arrives over realtime vd_status_<rowId>
flatCases.preconditions: Successful activate (status push_now); the row is processed by the push pipeline.
steps: Tap Push and stay on the detail sheet.
Wait for the Tally push to complete.
flatCases.expected: The vd_status_<rowId> channel (push_queue UPDATE filtered eq id) delivers the terminal result; sale shows a success/fail dialog when status becomes pushed/failed with tally_response. UI does not poll.

flatCases.title: Mismatched-length API key yields clean 401, not a crash
flatCases.preconditions: Build with an x-api-key whose byte length differs from the backend's expected key.
steps: Send activate (or reorder) with a deliberately shorter/longer key.
Observe response.
flatCases.expected: requireApiKey/requireClientApiKey check buffer length before timingSafeEqual, so a length mismatch returns a clean 401 Unauthorized instead of throwing (timingSafeEqual would otherwise throw on unequal lengths).

flatCases.title: Reorder report happy path returns CSV from client Supabase
flatCases.preconditions: Signed in; client Supabase (SUPABASE_URL_Client) has a single 'K V ENTERPRISES' company with reorder data; backend API_KEY_CLIENT == mrpApiKey.
steps: Open a report category with a valid reportId.
Wait for the CSV to load and render.
flatCases.expected: getRaw('/api/sync/reorder-levels/<reportId>', {company_name:'K V ENTERPRISES', format:'csv'}) returns 200 CSV; report renders. Data is sourced from reorderSupabase, not the app's active SUPABASE_URL.

flatCases.title: Reorder route ignores Firebase Bearer and authenticates by API_KEY_CLIENT only
flatCases.preconditions: Signed in (valid Bearer) but build where mrpApiKey != API_KEY_CLIENT.
steps: Open a report.
Capture the request headers and response.
flatCases.expected: requireClientApiKey checks ONLY x-api-key vs API_KEY_CLIENT and ignores the Bearer; if mrpApiKey != API_KEY_CLIENT the route returns 401 even though the user is validly signed in. Confirms Bearer is not honored here.

flatCases.title: mrpApiKey (client publishable key) is used for reorder in ALL flavors
flatCases.preconditions: Testing-flavor build (app otherwise on yynuu).
steps: On a testing build, open a report.
Inspect which Supabase project the data comes from.
flatCases.expected: Even on the testing build, mrpApiKey is the ztugw/client publishable key (sb_publishable_IRsM...) and reorder reads from the SEPARATE client Supabase. The report reflects the client project's inventory, inconsistent with the yynuu queue/history the user otherwise sees.

flatCases.title: Hardcoded company_name='K V ENTERPRISES' yields 409 when duplicate company rows exist
flatCases.preconditions: Client Supabase has TWO 'K V ENTERPRISES' rows (known ztugw duplicate-company issue).
steps: Open any report category.
Observe the load result.
flatCases.expected: DEFECT TO FLAG: resolveCompanyLookup returns 409 (company resolution conflict) because of the duplicate rows; the report silently fails to load. The app hardcodes the company name with no override, so the user cannot recover in-app.

flatCases.title: Reorder 404 when company not found
flatCases.preconditions: Client Supabase has NO 'K V ENTERPRISES' row.
steps: Open a report.
Observe the result.
flatCases.expected: Backend returns 404 'company not found'; getRaw throws 'Request failed: 404' and reports to Sentry; the report screen shows a load error.

flatCases.title: Reorder 400 on invalid reportKey
flatCases.preconditions: Ability to request an invalid/unknown reportKey.
steps: Trigger getRaw with a malformed reportKey (e.g. unknown category).
Observe response.
flatCases.expected: Backend returns 400 'invalid reportKey'; getRaw throws 'Request failed: 400'; error surfaced to the user, Sentry event recorded.

flatCases.title: Reorder 401 on wrong client key
flatCases.preconditions: Build with mrpApiKey not equal to API_KEY_CLIENT (or missing).
steps: Open a report.
Observe response.
flatCases.expected: requireClientApiKey returns 401 Unauthorized; getRaw throws Exception('Unauthorized'). No report data leaks.

flatCases.title: Reorder 500 on report build error
flatCases.preconditions: Force the backend report builder to fail (e.g. malformed client data).
steps: Open a report that triggers a server-side build error.
Observe response.
flatCases.expected: Backend returns 500; getRaw throws 'Request failed: 500' and reports the body to Sentry; report screen shows an error state, no partial CSV.

flatCases.title: Web: report CSV is always refetched (no path_provider disk cache)
flatCases.preconditions: Web build; signed in; a working report.
steps: Open a report (first fetch).
Navigate away and reopen the same report.
Observe network calls.
flatCases.expected: On web, report_screen has no on-disk CSV cache (path_provider unsupported) so it refetches the reorder endpoint each time. No file is written to disk.

flatCases.title: Native: report CSV cached to disk after first fetch
flatCases.preconditions: Android build; signed in; a working report.
steps: Open a report (first fetch hits the network).
Reopen the same report.
Observe network vs disk read.
flatCases.expected: On Android the CSV is cached to disk on first fetch and read from file on subsequent opens (path_provider available); fewer network calls than web.

flatCases.title: Desktop breakpoint (>=900) shows side-rail; <900 shows phone bottom-nav
flatCases.preconditions: Web build on a resizable window.
steps: Open the app in a window >=900px wide.
Shrink the window below 900px.
flatCases.expected: At >=900 ScreenFrame renders _buildDesktop (AppSideNav rail width 96, full-width body, no centered card/cap). Below 900 it renders _buildPhone (centered 500px card + AppBottomNav). Layout switches live on resize.

flatCases.title: Camera/scanner tab hidden on web in BOTH bottom-nav and side-rail
flatCases.preconditions: Web build, signed in.
steps: View AppBottomNav (narrow window) and AppSideNav (wide window).
Look for the camera tab (index 2).
flatCases.expected: The camera index-2 tab is hidden in both navs on web via !(kIsWeb && index==2); other tabs keep their index mapping and remain navigable. No 'scan' entry point on web.

flatCases.title: Camera/scanner tab visible and functional on mobile
flatCases.preconditions: Android build, signed in.
steps: View the bottom nav.
Tap the camera tab (index 2).
flatCases.expected: On Android the camera tab is present and opens the ML Kit document scanner. (Document scanner is Android-only; web/iOS show 'only available on Android' if reached.)

flatCases.title: Web applies 1.4x text scaling to routes and modal sheets
flatCases.preconditions: Web build.
steps: Open several screens and a modal bottom sheet (e.g. voucher detail).
Compare text size to a mobile build at default scale.
flatCases.expected: MaterialApp.builder wraps the child in MediaQuery(textScaler: TextScaler.linear(1.4)) only when kIsWeb, so web text (including modal sheets) is 1.4x larger. Mobile uses default scaling.

flatCases.title: Web text is selectable/copyable via SelectionArea
flatCases.preconditions: Web build.
steps: On any screen, click-drag to select a Text label and copy it.
flatCases.expected: Text is selectable and copyable because home is wrapped in SelectionArea (web canvas text is otherwise non-selectable). On mobile this has no visible effect.

flatCases.title: Two-pane image+summary sheet on wide screen
flatCases.preconditions: Web build in a window >=900px; a push_queue row with a stored image.
steps: Open the voucher detail sheet for a row that has an image in a wide window.
Then shrink below 900 and reopen.
flatCases.expected: isWideScreen (>=900) drives a two-pane layout (image + summary side by side). Below 900 it falls back to a single-pane/stacked sheet. Image still streams via getBytes.

flatCases.title: ResponsiveCenter caps form width at 440 on wide screens only
flatCases.preconditions: Any build; a form screen.
steps: View a form on a >=900px wide window/desktop.
View the same form on a narrow phone window.
flatCases.expected: On wide screens forms are capped at kFormMaxWidth 440 and centered; on phone widths they fill the 500px card. No edge-to-edge stretched form on desktop.

flatCases.title: Live window resize across 900px swaps layout without restart
flatCases.preconditions: Web build open in a resizable browser window.
steps: Start at ~1200px (desktop layout).
Slowly drag the window narrower past 900px and back.
Observe nav and content reflow.
flatCases.expected: LayoutBuilder/MediaQuery recompute on resize: side-rail<->bottom-nav and full-width<->card swap occur live at the 900 boundary with no crash, no lost navigation state.

flatCases.title: Web has no file share / on-disk image cache
flatCases.preconditions: Web build; a row with an image.
steps: Open an invoice image on web.
Look for a 'share file' / 'save to disk' affordance and reopen to check caching.
flatCases.expected: No file-share option and no on-disk image cache on web (path_provider unsupported); image bytes are re-fetched each open. On Android these would be available.

flatCases.title: Sentry is a no-op when DSN is empty (bare build)
flatCases.preconditions: Build with no SENTRY_DSN (bare/default).
steps: Run the app and trigger an error path (force a backend failure).
Observe app behavior and confirm no events are sent.
flatCases.expected: With Config.sentryDsn='' the SentryFlutter.init, reportFailure, and reportHandledError are all behaviour-neutral no-ops; the app behaves exactly as before and no events are emitted. (Note: all three env files DO set a DSN, so only a bare build is a no-op.)

flatCases.title: Failed push/report has app-side Sentry event but no correlated server event
flatCases.preconditions: Build with DSN; force an activate or report failure.
steps: Force an activate 409/500 or a report 500.
In Sentry, find the app event by request_id.
Search the backend for a correlated event with the same request_id.
flatCases.expected: DEFECT TO FLAG: Only the app-side event exists (tagged request_id/endpoint/status). The backend has no Sentry and ignores x-request-id, so there is no server-side counterpart. Push/report failures cannot be traced end-to-end.

flatCases.title: SentryHttpClient records a breadcrumb per backend request
flatCases.preconditions: Build with DSN; signed in.
steps: Make several ApiClient calls.
Then trigger a crash/error and inspect the Sentry event breadcrumbs.
flatCases.expected: Each request leaves an http breadcrumb (captureFailedRequests is OFF, breadcrumbs ON) so the captured event carries recent call history; sentry-trace is propagated when a span is active.

flatCases.title: Handled Supabase errors reported via reportHandledError
flatCases.preconditions: Build with DSN; a direct Supabase op that fails (e.g. RLS denial or 400).
steps: Trigger a direct Supabase read/write that returns a handled error.
Inspect Sentry.
flatCases.expected: The handled Supabase error is captured via reportHandledError (not a crash) and appears in Sentry; the app continues without crashing.

flatCases.title: Cross-project JWT mismatch: prod app on b60ed against 366 backend -> Bearer routes 401, key routes still work
flatCases.preconditions: FLAVOR=prod build (Firebase=aiaccountant-b60ed) hitting the 366 backend whose FIREBASE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_B64 targets a different Firebase project.
steps: Sign in (real prod Firebase) on a prod build.
Call a Bearer-authed endpoint (image fetch via getBytes).
Then call an x-api-key-only endpoint (activate, reorder).
flatCases.expected: DEFECT TO FLAG: the 366 backend cannot verify a b60ed-issued token, so Bearer-authed routes (image fetch) return 401, while x-api-key-only routes (activate, reorder) still succeed. Partial silent breakage where some features work and some 401 with no clear cause.

flatCases.title: Two clients on different flavors operate on different Supabase projects (env isolation)
flatCases.preconditions: Same user signed in on a testing build (yynuu) and a deployment build (ztugw) simultaneously.
steps: Sign in as the same account on both the testing and deployment builds.
Create/observe a push_queue row on each.
Check whether rows appear on the other client.
flatCases.expected: The two builds talk to different Supabase projects (yynuu vs ztugw), so realtime/queue changes do NOT cross between them. Confirms env-split data isolation — a user must use the correct flavor to see their real data.

flatCases.title: Both clients on the SAME flavor see each other's realtime changes (phone + web)
flatCases.preconditions: Same flavor (same Supabase project), same user, signed in on Android and web at once.
steps: Sign in on Android and on web (same flavor).
On Android, push a voucher (activate -> push_now).
Observe the web client's queue/status without manual refresh.
flatCases.expected: Because both point at the same Supabase project, realtime (e.g. push_queue / vd_status_<rowId>) propagates the change to the other client live. No env mismatch; data stays consistent across devices.

flatCases.title: Wrong SUPABASE_URL/flavor sends all direct reads/writes/realtime to the wrong project
flatCases.preconditions: A build whose SUPABASE_URL/anon key were misconfigured (e.g. prod.json placeholder, or a typo).
steps: Build with a mismatched SUPABASE_URL (e.g. prod flavor pointing at yynuu).
Sign in and create a push_queue row / load history.
Verify which project actually stores the data.
flatCases.expected: DEFECT TO FLAG: every direct Supabase read/write and all realtime channels hit whatever SUPABASE_URL is compiled in. A wrong value (the prod placeholder pointing at yynuu) means a 'prod' user silently operates on TESTING data. Must be validated before any prod release.

flatCases.title: In-flight token refresh during a backend call does not duplicate or corrupt the request
flatCases.preconditions: Signed in near token-expiry; ability to trigger a backend call while the token refreshes.
steps: Trigger an ApiClient.get exactly as the Firebase ID token is refreshing.
Observe the request's Authorization header and result.
flatCases.expected: _headers awaits getIdToken() which returns a fresh token; the single request carries a valid Bearer and completes once. No duplicate fire or stale-token 401 storm.

flatCases.title: Same x-request-id format is unique per call (no collisions under rapid calls)
flatCases.preconditions: Ability to observe outgoing headers for many rapid calls.
steps: Fire several ApiClient calls in quick succession.
Collect the x-request-id values.
flatCases.expected: newRequestId() = microsecond-timestamp-hex + random-hex; values are unique across rapid calls. (Cosmetic: even if duplicated, backend ignores it, but uniqueness aids app-side Sentry grouping.)
